rules.rule_name: Initialize Program Working Areas
rules.rule_description: Before any processing begins, all working storage fields including queue names, message buffers, and error display areas must be cleared to ensure no residual data affects processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
1: Program Initialization
Initialize working storage fields,
clear queue names and message buffers

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has been triggered and is starting execution
acceptance_criteria.When: The program begins its initialization phase
acceptance_criteria.Then: The input queue name, queue manager name, queue message buffer, and MQ error display area must all be cleared to spaces before any queue operations are attempted

rules.rule_name: Open Error Queue Before All Other Processing
rules.rule_description: The error queue CARD.DEMO.ERROR must be opened for writing as the very first queue operation, before any other queues are opened, so that all subsequent errors can be captured and reported.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
2: Open Error Queue
Open CARD.DEMO.ERROR for
writing error messages

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has completed initialization of working storage fields
acceptance_criteria.When: The program attempts to open the error queue named CARD.DEMO.ERROR for output
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the queue opens successfully, the error queue handle is saved and the error queue is marked as open for use throughout the program; if the queue fails to open, the error details are displayed and the program terminates immediately without processing any messages

rules.rule_name: Retrieve MQ Trigger Message to Determine Input Queue
rules.rule_description: The program is activated by an MQ trigger mechanism. It must retrieve the CICS trigger message to dynamically determine which input queue contains the date request messages to be processed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
3: Retrieve Transaction Trigger Information
Retrieve MQ trigger message from CICS
to obtain input queue name

acceptance_criteria.Given: The error queue has been successfully opened and the program is ready to begin message processing
acceptance_criteria.When: The program retrieves the CICS trigger message into the MQTM trigger message structure
acceptance_criteria.Then: The trigger message is retrieved and the program evaluates whether the retrieval was successful before proceeding to extract the input queue name

rules.rule_name: Validate Trigger Message Retrieval Success
rules.rule_description: The program must validate that the CICS trigger message was successfully retrieved before attempting to extract queue names and process messages. If retrieval fails, an error must be reported and processing must stop.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Trigger Retrieved
Successfully?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has attempted to retrieve the CICS trigger message
acceptance_criteria.When: The CICS response code is evaluated
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the response is NORMAL, the program extracts the input queue name from the trigger message field MQTM-QNAME and sets the reply queue to CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE; if the response is not NORMAL, the program records the error paragraph as 'CICS RETRIEVE', formats the response codes into an error message string, sends the error to the error queue, and terminates immediately

rules.rule_name: Set Input and Reply Queue Names from Trigger
rules.rule_description: Upon successful trigger retrieval, the input queue name is dynamically assigned from the trigger message, while the reply queue is always fixed to CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE regardless of the request source.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
4: Set Input and Reply Queue Names
Set input queue from trigger message
Set reply queue to CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE

acceptance_criteria.Given: The CICS trigger message has been successfully retrieved
acceptance_criteria.When: The program extracts queue name information from the trigger message
acceptance_criteria.Then: The input queue name must be set to the value of MQTM-QNAME from the trigger message, and the reply queue name must always be set to the hardcoded value 'CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE'

rules.rule_name: Open Input Queue for Reading Date Requests
rules.rule_description: The dynamically determined input queue must be opened for shared reading to allow multiple consumers to access it simultaneously, enabling the program to retrieve incoming date request messages.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
5: Open Input Queue
Open designated input MQ queue
for reading date request messages

acceptance_criteria.Given: The input queue name has been set from the trigger message
acceptance_criteria.When: The program attempts to open the input queue for shared reading
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the queue opens successfully, the input queue handle is saved and the input queue is marked as open; if the queue fails to open, the queue name and error 'INP MQOPEN ERR' are recorded, the error is sent to the error queue, and the program terminates

rules.rule_name: Open Output Reply Queue for Writing Date Responses
rules.rule_description: The fixed reply queue CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE must be opened for writing before any date/time responses can be sent back to requesting applications.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
6: Open Output/Reply Queue
Open CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE
for writing date/time responses

acceptance_criteria.Given: The input queue has been successfully opened and the reply queue name is set to CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE
acceptance_criteria.When: The program attempts to open the reply queue for output
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the queue opens successfully, the output queue handle is saved and the reply queue is marked as open; if the queue fails to open, the queue name and error 'OUT MQOPEN ERR' are recorded, the error is sent to the error queue, and the program terminates

rules.rule_name: Retrieve Next Date Request Message with Wait
rules.rule_description: The program retrieves the next available date request message from the input queue, waiting up to 5 seconds for a message to arrive before concluding that no more messages are available.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
7: Get Request Message
Read next available request message
from input queue - 5 second wait

acceptance_criteria.Given: The input queue is open and the program is ready to retrieve messages
acceptance_criteria.When: The program attempts to read the next message from the input queue
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program must wait up to 5000 milliseconds (5 seconds) for a message; the message buffer size is set to 1000 bytes; message ID and correlation ID filters are cleared so any available message is retrieved; if a message is retrieved it is made available for processing; if no message arrives within 5 seconds the no-more-messages condition is set

rules.rule_name: Determine Whether More Messages Exist for Processing
rules.rule_description: After each message retrieval attempt, the program must determine whether a message was successfully obtained to decide whether to continue processing or proceed to orderly shutdown.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
More Messages
Available?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has attempted to retrieve a message from the input queue
acceptance_criteria.When: The result of the message retrieval is evaluated
acceptance_criteria.Then: If a message is available, the program saves the message identifiers and proceeds to retrieve the current date and time; if no more messages are available, the program proceeds directly to close the input queue and begin orderly termination

rules.rule_name: Save Message Identifiers for Reply Correlation
rules.rule_description: When a request message is received, its message ID and correlation ID must be saved so that the reply can be correlated back to the original request by the calling application.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
8: Save Message Identifiers
Save message ID, correlation ID,
and reply-to queue from request

acceptance_criteria.Given: A date request message has been successfully retrieved from the input queue
acceptance_criteria.When: The program processes the incoming message header
acceptance_criteria.Then: The message ID (MQMD-MSGID) must be saved to SAVE-MSGID and the correlation ID (MQMD-CORRELID) must be saved to SAVE-CORELID so they can be used when sending the reply message

rules.rule_name: Retrieve Current System Date and Time
rules.rule_description: For each date request message received, the program must obtain the current system date and time as the source data for constructing the date/time reply.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
9: Get Current System Date and Time
Retrieve current system date and time
using CICS ASKTIME

acceptance_criteria.Given: A date request message has been received and message identifiers have been saved
acceptance_criteria.When: The program requests the current system timestamp
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current absolute system time must be retrieved into WS-ABS-TIME for subsequent formatting into human-readable date and time values

rules.rule_name: Format System Date and Time into Readable Format
rules.rule_description: The raw system timestamp must be formatted into a standardized human-readable date format of MM-DD-YYYY with a dash separator and a time format with time separators before being included in the reply message.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
10: Format Date and Time
Format timestamp into MM-DD-YYYY
and HH:MM:SS using CICS FORMATTIME

acceptance_criteria.Given: The current system absolute time has been retrieved into WS-ABS-TIME
acceptance_criteria.When: The program formats the timestamp
acceptance_criteria.Then: The date must be formatted as MM-DD-YYYY using a dash ('-') as the date separator and stored in WS-MMDDYYYY; the time must be formatted with time separators and stored in WS-TIME

rules.rule_name: Construct Date and Time Reply Message
rules.rule_description: The formatted date and time values must be combined into a standardized reply message string that clearly labels both the system date and system time for the requesting application.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
11: Build Date/Time Reply Message
Construct reply: SYSTEM DATE: MM-DD-YYYY
SYSTEM TIME: HH:MM:SS

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system date has been formatted as MM-DD-YYYY in WS-MMDDYYYY and the system time has been formatted in WS-TIME
acceptance_criteria.When: The program constructs the reply message
acceptance_criteria.Then: The reply message must be built by concatenating the literal 'SYSTEM DATE : ' followed by WS-MMDDYYYY, then the literal 'SYSTEM TIME : ' followed by WS-TIME, all delimited by size, and stored in REPLY-MESSAGE

rules.rule_name: Send Date/Time Reply Correlated to Original Request
rules.rule_description: The constructed date/time reply message must be sent to the reply queue with the original request's message identifiers preserved, so the requesting application can match the reply to its original request.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
12: Send Reply Message
Put date/time reply onto output/reply
MQ queue correlated to original request

acceptance_criteria.Given: The date/time reply message has been constructed and the original message ID and correlation ID have been saved
acceptance_criteria.When: The program sends the reply message to the output queue CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE
acceptance_criteria.Then: The reply message must be placed in a 1000-byte buffer; the saved message ID (SAVE-MSGID) must be set as MQMD-MSGID and the saved correlation ID (SAVE-CORELID) must be set as MQMD-CORRELID on the outgoing message; the message format must be set to string; if the put operation succeeds the condition codes are recorded; if the put operation fails the queue name and error 'MQPUT ERR' are recorded, the error is sent to the error queue, and the program terminates

rules.rule_name: Commit Each Message Transaction Before Fetching Next
rules.rule_description: After each date request message has been processed and its reply sent, the transaction must be committed before retrieving the next message, ensuring each message is processed as an independent, atomic unit of work.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
14: Commit Transaction
Issue CICS syncpoint to commit
processed message transaction

acceptance_criteria.Given: A date request message has been fully processed and its date/time reply has been sent to the reply queue
acceptance_criteria.When: The program prepares to retrieve the next message
acceptance_criteria.Then: A CICS SYNCPOINT must be issued to commit the completed message transaction before the next message retrieval attempt, ensuring the reply is permanently written and the processed message is removed from the input queue

rules.rule_name: Continuous Message Processing Loop
rules.rule_description: The program must continuously cycle through committing the previous transaction and retrieving the next message until no more messages are available in the input queue.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
13: Process Message Loop
Continuously retrieve and process
date request messages

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program is in active message processing mode with input and output queues open
acceptance_criteria.When: The program completes processing of one date request message
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program must loop back to commit the transaction and attempt to retrieve the next message, continuing this cycle until the no-more-messages condition is detected, at which point the loop exits and termination begins

rules.rule_name: Send Error Notification to Error Queue
rules.rule_description: When any processing error occurs, the full error details must be written to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue to enable monitoring and alerting of failed operations.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
15: Send Error Notification
Write error details to
CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue

acceptance_criteria.Given: A processing error has occurred, including the error paragraph name, queue name, and error condition codes captured in the MQ error display area
acceptance_criteria.When: The program attempts to write the error notification to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue
acceptance_criteria.Then: The complete error display information must be moved to the error message buffer and placed onto the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue in a 1000-byte string-formatted message; if the error queue write itself fails, the error details are displayed to the system console and the program terminates immediately

rules.rule_name: Close Input Queue During Termination
rules.rule_description: During program termination, the input queue must be closed only if it was previously successfully opened, ensuring proper release of queue resources.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
16: Close Input Queue
Close input MQ queue
to release resources

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program is in the termination phase
acceptance_criteria.When: The program checks whether the input queue was opened
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the input queue is marked as open, the program must close it using the saved input queue handle; if the close operation fails, the error 'MQCLOSE ERR' is recorded and the program proceeds to termination

rules.rule_name: Close Output Reply Queue During Termination
rules.rule_description: During program termination, the output reply queue must be closed only if it was previously successfully opened, ensuring proper release of queue resources.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
17: Close Output/Reply Queue
Close output/reply MQ queue
to release resources

acceptance_criteria.Given: The input queue has been closed and the program continues termination
acceptance_criteria.When: The program checks whether the output reply queue was opened
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the reply queue is marked as open, the program must close it using the saved output queue handle; if the close operation fails, the error 'MQCLOSE ERR' is recorded and the program proceeds to termination

rules.rule_name: Close Error Queue During Termination
rules.rule_description: During program termination, the error queue must be closed only if it was previously successfully opened, ensuring all queue resources are properly released before returning control to CICS.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
18: Close Error Queue
Close error MQ queue
to release resources

acceptance_criteria.Given: The input and output queues have been closed and the program continues termination
acceptance_criteria.When: The program checks whether the error queue was opened
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the error queue is marked as open, the program must close it using the saved error queue handle; if the close operation fails, the error 'MQCLOSE ERR' is recorded, a final error notification is sent, and the program proceeds to termination

rules.rule_name: Return Control to CICS on Program Completion
rules.rule_description: After all queues have been closed, the program must formally return control to CICS to end the transaction, whether the termination was due to normal completion or an error condition.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
19: Program Termination
Return control to CICS
ending the transaction

acceptance_criteria.Given: All open queues have been closed during the termination phase
acceptance_criteria.When: The program has completed all cleanup activities
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program must issue a CICS RETURN command to formally end the CICS transaction and return control to the CICS transaction manager

rules.rule_name: Clear Input Queue Name Before Processing
rules.rule_description: Before any message processing begins, the input queue name must be cleared to spaces to ensure no residual or stale queue name from a previous execution is carried forward.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Clear Input Queue Name
Set to Spaces

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has just started execution and no queue connections have been established yet
acceptance_criteria.When: The program initializes its working storage fields at the start of a new processing cycle
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Input Queue Name field must be set to spaces (blank), ensuring no previously held or residual queue name value is present before the queue name is dynamically assigned from the trigger message

rules.rule_name: Clear Queue Manager Name Before Processing
rules.rule_description: Before any message processing begins, the Queue Manager Name must be cleared to spaces to ensure no stale or inherited value from a prior execution affects the current processing session.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Clear Queue Manager Name
Set to Spaces

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has just started execution and no queue manager connections have been established yet
acceptance_criteria.When: The program initializes its working storage fields at the start of a new processing cycle
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Queue Manager Name field must be set to spaces (blank), ensuring the queue manager name is clean and free of any residual value before processing begins

rules.rule_name: Clear Message Buffer Before Processing
rules.rule_description: Before any message processing begins, the message buffer (QUEUE-MESSAGE) must be cleared to spaces to ensure no leftover message content from a prior execution is present when the program starts reading new messages.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Clear Message Buffer
Set to Spaces

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has just started execution and no messages have been retrieved yet
acceptance_criteria.When: The program initializes its working storage fields at the start of a new processing cycle
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Queue Message buffer field must be set to spaces (blank), ensuring the message buffer contains no residual data before new messages are retrieved and processed

rules.rule_name: Initialize Error Display Area Before Processing
rules.rule_description: Before any message processing begins, the error display area (MQ-ERR-DISPLAY) must be reset to its default values to ensure any error information captured and reported during this execution session is fresh and not contaminated by data from a previous run.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Initialize Error Display Area
Reset to Default Values

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has just started execution and no errors have been encountered yet
acceptance_criteria.When: The program initializes its working storage fields at the start of a new processing cycle
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Error Display Area (MQ-ERR-DISPLAY) must be initialized to its default values (numeric fields reset to zeroes, alphanumeric fields reset to spaces), ensuring all error tracking fields are clean before any error conditions can be encountered during processing

key_functionalities.title: Open Error Queue
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD

    B[Set Error Queue Name\nto CARD.DEMO.ERROR]

    E[Mark Error Queue\nas Open and Ready\nto Receive Error Messages]
    F[Display Error Details\nto System Log]
    G([Proceed to Retrieve\nTransaction Trigger])
    H([Program Termination])

    A --> B
    B --> C
    C --> D
    D -->|Yes| E
    E --> G
    D -->|No - Unable to Open\nError Queue| F
    F --> H

rules.rule_name: Assign Dedicated Error Queue Name
rules.rule_description: The program must use a fixed, designated queue named CARD.DEMO.ERROR as the sole destination for all error messages generated during processing. This queue name is a system-wide constant and is assigned before any queue access is attempted.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Error Queue Name to CARD.DEMO.ERROR

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has started and is preparing to open the error reporting channel
acceptance_criteria.When: The error queue is being initialized at the start of the program
acceptance_criteria.Then: The error queue name must be set to 'CARD.DEMO.ERROR' as the designated error message destination

rules.rule_name: Request Access to Error Queue for Writing Error Messages
rules.rule_description: The program must establish write access to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue before any business processing begins. The queue must be opened with output capability, allowing the program to write error messages to it throughout the processing lifecycle.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Request Access to CARD.DEMO.ERROR Queue for Writing Error Messages

acceptance_criteria.Given: The error queue name has been set to 'CARD.DEMO.ERROR' and the program is ready to establish queue access
acceptance_criteria.When: The program requests write access to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must attempt to open the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue with output (write) permissions so that error messages can be sent to it during processing

rules.rule_name: Mark Error Queue as Open and Ready Upon Successful Access
rules.rule_description: When the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue is successfully opened for writing, the program must record the queue's active connection handle and flag the error queue as available. This readiness flag is used throughout the program to determine whether error messages can be dispatched and whether the queue needs to be closed during termination.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark Error Queue as Open and Ready to Receive Error Messages

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has requested write access to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue
acceptance_criteria.When: The queue is opened successfully without any errors
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program must save the active connection reference to the error queue and mark the error queue status as 'Open and Ready', enabling error message delivery for the remainder of the program's execution

rules.rule_name: Terminate Program When Error Queue Cannot Be Opened
rules.rule_description: If the program is unable to open the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue for writing, it cannot safely handle any subsequent errors that may arise during processing. In this case, the program must log the failure details to the system and immediately terminate, as continuing without an error reporting channel would leave any future errors undetected and unreported.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Error Details to System Log

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has requested write access to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue
acceptance_criteria.When: The queue cannot be opened due to any failure condition
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program must record the name of the queue that failed to open ('CARD.DEMO.ERROR') along with the failure description ('ERR MQOPEN ERR') and all associated error details to the system log, and then immediately terminate all processing without proceeding to any further business operations

rules.rule_name: Retrieve MQ Trigger Message from CICS Transaction Start Data
rules.rule_description: When this program is initiated by a CICS transaction trigger, it must retrieve the trigger message that contains the identity of the input queue to be processed. This trigger message is the entry point that drives all subsequent processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Request MQ Trigger Message from CICS Transaction Start Data

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has been started by a CICS transaction trigger event and the error queue CARD.DEMO.ERROR has been successfully opened
acceptance_criteria.When: The program requests the MQ trigger message from the CICS transaction start data
acceptance_criteria.Then: The trigger message content (MQTM) is retrieved and made available for extraction of the input queue name, along with response indicators that confirm whether the retrieval was successful or not

rules.rule_name: Validate Successful Retrieval of Trigger Message
rules.rule_description: After requesting the trigger message from CICS, the program must verify that the retrieval completed successfully before attempting to extract any queue information. Only a normal response code confirms a valid trigger message was received.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Trigger Message Retrieved Successfully?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has submitted a request to retrieve the MQ trigger message from CICS transaction start data
acceptance_criteria.When: The CICS response code is evaluated after the retrieval attempt
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the response code indicates a Normal (successful) completion, the program proceeds to extract the input queue name from the trigger message; otherwise, the program treats the retrieval as a failure and initiates error handling

rules.rule_name: Extract Input Queue Name from Trigger Message
rules.rule_description: Upon successful retrieval of the trigger message, the program extracts the name of the input queue that initiated this transaction. This queue name is dynamic and varies per trigger event, determining which queue the program will read messages from during this execution.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Extract Input Queue Name from Trigger Message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The MQ trigger message has been successfully retrieved from CICS transaction start data

rules.rule_name: Assign Fixed Reply Queue for Date-Time Responses

rules.rule_name: Record Trigger Message Retrieval Failure Details
rules.rule_description: When the trigger message cannot be successfully retrieved from CICS, the program must capture and record the full details of the failure, including the source operation that failed and both response codes, so that the error can be fully diagnosed and reported.

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has attempted to retrieve the MQ trigger message from CICS transaction start data

acceptance_criteria.Then: The program records the failure by: (1) identifying the failed operation as 'CICS RETRIEVE', (2) capturing the primary CICS response code, (3) capturing the secondary CICS response code, and (4) constructing a combined error message containing the label 'RESP: ' followed by both response code values, to be used in the error notification

rules.rule_name: Send Trigger Retrieval Error Notification and Terminate
rules.rule_description: When the trigger message retrieval fails, the program must send a full error notification to the designated error queue so that operations teams are alerted, and then immediately terminate all processing since no valid input queue name is available to continue.

acceptance_criteria.Given: The trigger message retrieval has failed and the failure details including the operation name 'CICS RETRIEVE' and both response codes have been recorded in the error message
acceptance_criteria.When: The program invokes the error notification process followed by the termination process
acceptance_criteria.Then: The complete error details are sent as a message to the error queue CARD.DEMO.ERROR, and the program immediately terminates by closing all open queues (input queue if open, output reply queue if open, error queue if open) and returning control to CICS — no further message processing occurs

rules.rule_description: The input queue name is not hardcoded but is dynamically sourced from the trigger message retrieved at program startup. Before requesting access, the queue manager name is cleared and the trigger-provided queue name is assigned as the target input queue.

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has successfully retrieved the trigger message and extracted the input queue name (INPUT-QUEUE-NAME) from the trigger message field MQTM-QNAME
acceptance_criteria.When: The program prepares to open the input queue for reading incoming date request messages
acceptance_criteria.Then: The queue manager name field (MQOD-OBJECTQMGRNAME) is cleared to spaces and the dynamically retrieved INPUT-QUEUE-NAME is assigned as the target object name (MQOD-OBJECTNAME) for the open request

rules.rule_name: Request Shared Read Access to Input Queue

acceptance_criteria.When: The program requests access to open the input queue
acceptance_criteria.Then: The queue must be opened with the following combined access permissions: shared input reading (allowing multiple readers), save-all-context (preserving full message context for correlation), and fail-if-quiescing (preventing reads during queue manager shutdown)

rules.rule_name: Mark Input Queue as Ready When Successfully Opened
rules.rule_description: When the input queue is successfully opened, the program records the queue handle for subsequent message retrieval operations and marks the input queue status as open and available, enabling the rest of the program to proceed with reading date request messages.

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has requested access to the input queue

acceptance_criteria.Then: The returned queue handle (MQ-HOBJ) is saved as INPUT-QUEUE-HANDLE for use in subsequent message read operations, the condition code and reason code are recorded, and the input queue status flag (REPLY-QUEUE-OPEN) is set to TRUE to indicate the queue is open and available for reading

rules.rule_name: Capture Error Details When Input Queue Cannot Be Opened
rules.rule_description: When the input queue cannot be opened for any reason, the program captures the full error context including the queue name that failed and a descriptive error message, so that the failure can be reported and investigated.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has requested access to the input queue
acceptance_criteria.When: The input queue fails to open (condition code is anything other than MQCC-OK)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The condition code and reason code from the failed open attempt are recorded, the INPUT-QUEUE-NAME is captured in the error queue name field (MQ-APPL-QUEUE-NAME), and the error description 'INP MQOPEN ERR' is recorded in the error return message field (MQ-APPL-RETURN-MESSAGE)

rules.rule_name: Send Error Notification to Error Queue When Input Queue Unavailable

acceptance_criteria.When: The program handles the input queue open failure
acceptance_criteria.Then: The error details are written to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue by invoking the error notification process (9000-ERROR), which places the full error display information into the error queue as a 1000-byte message with string format

rules.rule_name: Terminate Program After Input Queue Open Failure
rules.rule_description: When the input queue cannot be opened, the program cannot fulfill its purpose of processing date request messages. Therefore, after sending the error notification, the program must close any queues that were already opened and terminate, preventing any partial or incomplete processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:

acceptance_criteria.Given: The input queue has failed to open, error details have been recorded, and the error notification has been sent to CARD.DEMO.ERROR
acceptance_criteria.When: The program proceeds to termination after an input queue open failure
acceptance_criteria.Then: The termination process (8000-TERMINATION) is invoked, which closes the error queue (CARD.DEMO.ERROR) if it was previously opened, and then returns control to CICS, ending the program without processing any date request messages

rules.rule_description: The program always uses a fixed, hardcoded reply queue named CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE as the destination for all date/time response messages, regardless of the input queue or requestor identity.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Target Queue: CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has successfully retrieved the trigger message and identified the input queue to process
acceptance_criteria.When: The program prepares to open the output channel for sending date/time responses
acceptance_criteria.Then: The reply queue destination must always be set to 'CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE' — this value is fixed and cannot be overridden by any runtime input or trigger message content

rules.rule_name: Open Reply Queue for Writing Date/Time Response Messages
rules.rule_description: The program must open the reply queue CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE in write/output mode so that formatted date and time response messages can be delivered to requestors.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Open Queue for Writing Date/Time Responses

acceptance_criteria.Given: The reply queue name has been set to 'CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE' and the error queue is already open
acceptance_criteria.When: The program attempts to open the reply queue for writing date/time responses
acceptance_criteria.Then: The queue must be opened in output (write) mode with full message context passing enabled, so that response messages carry the complete originating context of the request

rules.rule_name: Mark Reply Queue as Ready When Successfully Opened
rules.rule_description: When the reply queue CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE is successfully opened, the program records the queue handle and marks the reply queue as available, enabling subsequent date/time response messages to be written.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Reply Queue Ready to Accept Date/Time Response Messages

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has attempted to open the reply queue 'CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE' for writing

acceptance_criteria.Then: The reply queue handle must be saved for use in subsequent message write operations, and the reply queue status must be flagged as 'open and ready' so that the program can proceed to retrieve and process incoming requests

rules.rule_name: Capture Error Details When Reply Queue Cannot Be Opened
rules.rule_description: If the reply queue CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE cannot be opened, the program must capture the failure details including the error condition code, reason code, the queue name that failed, and a descriptive error message to support diagnosis.

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has attempted to open the reply queue 'CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE' for writing date/time responses
acceptance_criteria.When: The queue open operation fails for any reason
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program must record the error condition code, the error reason code, the name of the queue that failed ('CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE'), and set the error description to 'OUT MQOPEN ERR' to identify this as an output queue open failure

rules.rule_name: Send Error Notification to Error Queue on Reply Queue Open Failure
rules.rule_description: When the reply queue CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE cannot be opened, the program must route the captured error details to the designated error queue (CARD.DEMO.ERROR) so that operations teams are notified of the failure.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Send Error Notification to Error Queue

acceptance_criteria.Given: The reply queue 'CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE' has failed to open and error details (error code, reason code, queue name, error description 'OUT MQOPEN ERR') have been captured
acceptance_criteria.When: The program processes the queue open failure
acceptance_criteria.Then: The full error details must be sent as a message to the error queue 'CARD.DEMO.ERROR' to notify operations of the reply queue open failure before the program terminates

rules.rule_name: Terminate Program When Reply Queue Cannot Be Opened
rules.rule_description: If the reply queue CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE cannot be opened, the program cannot deliver any date/time responses and must perform an orderly termination after sending the error notification, closing all previously opened queues.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: End: Program Termination Due to Queue Open Failure

acceptance_criteria.Given: The reply queue 'CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE' has failed to open and the error notification has been sent to the error queue
acceptance_criteria.When: The program completes error notification for the reply queue open failure
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program must immediately stop all processing, close any queues that were successfully opened prior to this failure (including the input queue and error queue), and return control — no date/time request messages will be processed during this execution

rules.rule_name: Set Message Wait Interval Before Reading Input Queue

rules.rule_name: Set Message Buffer Size for Input Queue Read

rules.rule_name: Clear Message Identifiers Before Reading New Message

rules.rule_name: Read Next Available Request Message from Input Queue

rules.rule_name: Save Message Identifiers Upon Successful Message Retrieval
rules.rule_description: When a message is successfully retrieved from the input queue, the program must capture and preserve the Message ID and Correlation ID from the incoming message. These identifiers are required later to correctly correlate the reply message back to the original request.

acceptance_criteria.Then: The Message ID (MQMD-MSGID) must be saved into SAVE-MSGID and the Correlation ID (MQMD-CORRELID) must be saved into SAVE-CORELID so they can be used when sending the reply message back to the requester

rules.rule_name: Proceed to Date/Time Processing After Message Retrieval

rules.rule_name: End Message Processing When No More Messages Are Available

rules.rule_name: Send Error Notification on Unexpected Message Retrieval Failure

acceptance_criteria.Then: The program must capture the error condition code and reason code, record the input queue name as the source of the error, set the error message to identify the failure, send the full error details to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR error queue via the 9000-ERROR routine, and then proceed to the termination step (8000-TERMINATION) to close all open queues and end processing

rules.rule_name: Save Incoming Correlation ID for Reply Tracking

rules.rule_name: Fixed Reply-To Queue Assignment for Date-Time Responses
rules.rule_description: The destination queue for all date and time responses is always fixed to CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE, regardless of the content of the incoming request message. This queue name is assigned at program startup when the trigger message is received and does not vary per message.

rules.rule_name: All Message Identifiers Must Be Present Before Reply Is Sent
rules.rule_description: Before a date and time reply message can be dispatched, all three required identifiers — Message ID, Correlation ID, and Reply-To Queue — must be available and populated. These identifiers together ensure the reply is correctly routed and correlated to the original request.

acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must immediately proceed to retrieve the next request message from the input queue, waiting up to 5000 milliseconds for a message to arrive, before repeating the process-and-commit cycle

rules.rule_name: Repeat Commit and Retrieve Cycle Until No More Messages Remain
rules.rule_description: The system continuously repeats the cycle of committing the current transaction and retrieving the next message until the input queue is exhausted (no more messages are available). Each message is treated as an independent unit of work.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Continue to Next
Message Processing

acceptance_criteria.Given: The input queue has been successfully opened and at least one message has been retrieved and processed
acceptance_criteria.When: The commit-and-retrieve cycle completes for each message
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must continue repeating the transaction commit followed by next-message retrieval until the NO-MORE-MSGS condition is reached, at which point the processing loop ends and the program proceeds to orderly termination

flowchart TD
    A([Error Condition Detected]) --> B

    B[Collect Error Details\nError Description, Condition Code,\nReason Code, Queue Name]

rules.rule_name: Collect Error Details for Notification
rules.rule_description: When an error condition is detected during processing, the system collects all relevant error details including the error description, condition code, reason code, and the name of the queue where the error occurred, and consolidates them into a single error notification message.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Collect Error Details
Error Description, Condition Code,
Reason Code, Queue Name

acceptance_criteria.Given: An error condition has been detected during queue processing or message handling, and the error details are available including: an error description (e.g., 'INP MQOPEN ERR', 'OUT MQOPEN ERR', 'MQPUT ERR'), a condition code, a reason code, and the name of the queue involved
acceptance_criteria.When: The error handling process is triggered by any queue operation failure (open, put, or close)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must collect and store: the error description into MQ-APPL-RETURN-MESSAGE, the condition code into MQ-APPL-CONDITION-CODE, the reason code into MQ-APPL-REASON-CODE, and the queue name into MQ-APPL-QUEUE-NAME; then combine all these details from MQ-ERR-DISPLAY into a single error notification message (ERROR-MESSAGE) ready for dispatch to the error queue

rules.rule_name: Write Error Notification to Error Queue
rules.rule_description: The consolidated error notification message must be written to the designated error queue CARD.DEMO.ERROR so that errors are centrally captured and available for monitoring and alerting.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Write Error Message to
CARD.DEMO.ERROR Queue

acceptance_criteria.Given: An error notification message has been prepared containing all error details (error description, condition code, reason code, queue name), the error queue CARD.DEMO.ERROR is open and available, and the message buffer is set to 1000 bytes with string format
acceptance_criteria.When: The system attempts to write the error notification message to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue using the MQPUT operation with syncpoint and default context options
acceptance_criteria.Then: The error message must be successfully placed onto the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue; the condition code and reason code from the write operation must be recorded; if the write is successful, control returns to the calling process

rules.rule_name: Handle Successful Error Notification Delivery
rules.rule_description: After attempting to write the error notification to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue, the system evaluates whether the write was successful and records the outcome accordingly.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Error Message
Written Successfully?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has attempted to write an error notification message to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue
acceptance_criteria.When: The MQPUT operation to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue completes and returns a condition code of OK (success)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system records the successful condition code and reason code, and returns control to the calling process that originally triggered the error handling

rules.rule_name: Handle Failed Error Notification Delivery
rules.rule_description: If the system is unable to write the error notification to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue, it must display the error details locally and immediately terminate all processing to prevent further data integrity issues.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: No - Queue Write Failed

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has attempted to write an error notification message to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue, and the MQPUT operation has returned a condition code other than OK (failure)
acceptance_criteria.When: The write to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue fails for any reason
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must: record the failed condition code and reason code, record the error queue name (CARD.DEMO.ERROR) as the queue where the failure occurred, record 'MQPUT ERR' as the error description, display the full error details locally (MQ-ERR-DISPLAY), and immediately initiate program termination by closing all open queues and stopping all processing

rules.rule_name: Initiate Error Handling on Queue Operation Failure
rules.rule_description: Whenever a queue operation (opening input queue, opening output queue, or putting a reply message) fails, the system must immediately invoke the error notification process before proceeding to termination.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Error Condition Detected

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is performing a queue operation such as opening the input queue, opening the output queue, or putting a reply message onto a queue
acceptance_criteria.When: Any queue operation returns a condition code other than OK (i.e., the operation did not succeed)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must immediately invoke the error notification process (9000-ERROR) to capture and dispatch the error details to CARD.DEMO.ERROR, followed by invoking the termination process (8000-TERMINATION) to close all open queues and stop processing

rules.rule_name: Identify Input Queue for Closure
rules.rule_description: Before closing the input queue, the program identifies the correct queue by associating the input queue name with its active queue handle to ensure the correct queue is targeted for closure.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Identify Input Queue
for Closure

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has completed processing messages or encountered an error requiring termination, and the input queue was previously opened successfully
acceptance_criteria.When: The program prepares to close the input queue
acceptance_criteria.Then: The input queue name (dynamically assigned from the trigger message) and its corresponding active queue handle are identified and set as the target for the close operation, with no-options (MQCO-NONE) applied indicating a standard close with no special behavior

rules.rule_name: Request to Close Input Queue
rules.rule_description: The program submits a formal request to the messaging system to close the input queue using the established queue connection and handle.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Request to Close
Input Queue

acceptance_criteria.Given: The input queue name and its active queue handle have been identified, and the queue connection handle is active
acceptance_criteria.When: The program issues a close request to the messaging system (MQCLOSE) using the queue connection handle, the input queue handle, and standard close options
acceptance_criteria.Then: The messaging system processes the close request and returns a condition code and reason code indicating the outcome of the closure attempt

rules.rule_name: Input Queue Closed Successfully
rules.rule_description: When the input queue is closed without errors, the program records the successful outcome and proceeds to close the output/reply queue as the next step in the orderly shutdown sequence.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Input Queue
Closed Successfully

acceptance_criteria.Given: A close request was submitted for the input queue
acceptance_criteria.When: The messaging system returns a successful condition code (MQCC-OK) for the close operation
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program records the successful condition code and reason code returned by the messaging system, and control returns to the termination routine to proceed with closing the output/reply queue next

rules.rule_name: Record Input Queue Close Failure Details
rules.rule_description: When the input queue cannot be closed successfully, the program captures all relevant failure information including the queue name and failure indicators to support error diagnosis and reporting.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Record Close
Failure Details

acceptance_criteria.Given: A close request was submitted for the input queue
acceptance_criteria.When: The messaging system returns a condition code other than success (not MQCC-OK) for the close operation
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program records the failure condition code, the failure reason code, the input queue name as the queue that failed to close, and sets the return message to 'MQCLOSE ERR' to identify the nature of the failure

rules.rule_name: Proceed to Program Termination on Close Failure
rules.rule_description: When the input queue fails to close, the program bypasses the normal sequential shutdown of remaining queues and immediately invokes the full termination routine to ensure the program ends in a controlled manner.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Proceed to
Program Termination

acceptance_criteria.Given: The input queue close operation has failed and failure details have been recorded
acceptance_criteria.When: The program determines it cannot successfully close the input queue
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program immediately invokes the termination routine (8000-TERMINATION), which will attempt to close any remaining open queues (output queue and error queue if still open) and return control to CICS, bypassing the normal sequential close of the output queue

rules.rule_name: Proceed to Close Output/Reply Queue After Input Queue Closure
rules.rule_description: After successfully closing the input queue, the program follows the defined shutdown sequence by proceeding to close the output/reply queue as the next step.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Proceed to Close
Output/Reply Queue

acceptance_criteria.Given: The input queue has been successfully closed
acceptance_criteria.When: Control returns to the termination routine after successful input queue closure
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program checks whether the output/reply queue (CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE) is marked as open, and if so, proceeds to close it as the next step in the orderly shutdown sequence

rules.rule_name: Initiate Closure of Reply Queue
rules.rule_description: When the program completes processing or encounters an error, it must attempt to close the reply queue CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE to release the queue resource.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Attempt to Close CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE Reply Queue

acceptance_criteria.Given: The output/reply queue CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE has been previously opened and is currently active
acceptance_criteria.When: The program reaches its termination phase, either after normal completion of all message processing or after encountering an error condition
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program must attempt to close the CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE reply queue using the stored output queue handle to release the queue resource

rules.rule_name: Confirm Successful Reply Queue Closure
rules.rule_description: After attempting to close the reply queue, the program evaluates whether the closure was successful and proceeds accordingly.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Queue Closed Successfully?

acceptance_criteria.Given: An attempt has been made to close the CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE reply queue
acceptance_criteria.When: The queue close operation returns a successful completion code
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program records the successful condition code and reason code, and the output/reply queue is considered successfully closed with no further action required

rules.rule_name: Capture Reply Queue Closure Failure Details
rules.rule_description: When the reply queue closure fails, the program must capture and record all relevant error details including the condition code, reason code, and the name of the queue that failed to close.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Record Error Details: Condition Code, Reason Code, Queue Name

acceptance_criteria.Given: An attempt has been made to close the CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE reply queue
acceptance_criteria.When: The queue close operation returns a failure condition code (any condition other than successful completion)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program must record the failure condition code, the failure reason code, and the queue name (CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE stored as input queue name) along with the error message 'MQCLOSE ERR' to identify the nature of the closure failure

rules.rule_name: Send Reply Queue Closure Error Notification
rules.rule_description: When the reply queue fails to close, the program must send a full error notification message containing the error details to the designated error queue CARD.DEMO.ERROR for monitoring and alerting purposes.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Send Error Notification to CARD.DEMO.ERROR

acceptance_criteria.Given: The reply queue CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE has failed to close and error details including condition code, reason code, queue name, and error message 'MQCLOSE ERR' have been recorded
acceptance_criteria.When: The error details are ready to be reported
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program must send the complete error information as a message to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue using the error queue handle, so that the failure is visible for operational monitoring and alerting

rules.rule_name: Proceed to Program Termination After Reply Queue Error
rules.rule_description: After sending the error notification for a reply queue closure failure, the program must proceed to the termination routine to ensure an orderly shutdown.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Proceed to Program Termination

acceptance_criteria.Given: The reply queue CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE has failed to close and the error notification has been sent to CARD.DEMO.ERROR
acceptance_criteria.When: The error notification has been successfully dispatched to the error queue
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program must immediately invoke the termination routine to perform an orderly shutdown, which includes closing any remaining open queues (input and error queues) and returning control back to the calling system

rules.rule_name: Conditional Execution of Reply Queue Closure
rules.rule_description: The reply queue closure is only attempted if the reply queue was successfully opened earlier in the program, preventing unnecessary closure attempts on queues that were never opened.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Close Output/Reply Queue - Close the output/reply MQ queue upon completion or error to release queue resources

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has reached its termination phase
acceptance_criteria.When: The program checks whether the reply queue CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE was successfully opened during initialization
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program must only attempt to close the reply queue if it was previously opened (RESP-QUEUE-OPEN flag is set to TRUE); if the queue was never opened, the closure step is skipped entirely

rules.sub_graph_node_text: Attempt to Close CARD.DEMO.ERROR Queue

acceptance_criteria.Given: The error queue named CARD.DEMO.ERROR is open and held by the program, and the program has reached the point of termination or completion
acceptance_criteria.When: The program initiates the closure of the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program must attempt to close the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue using the stored error queue handle and queue name

rules.rule_name: Confirm Successful Closure of Error Queue
rules.rule_description: When the error queue is successfully closed, the program acknowledges the successful release of the queue resource and records the outcome.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Queue Closed Successfully? → Yes → Error Queue Closed Resources Released Successfully

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has attempted to close the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue
acceptance_criteria.When: The queue closure operation completes successfully with no errors
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program records the successful condition code and reason code from the close operation, confirming that the error queue resources have been released successfully

rules.rule_name: Record Error Queue Closure Failure Details
rules.rule_description: When the error queue cannot be closed successfully, the program must capture and record all relevant failure details including the error description, condition code, reason code, and the name of the queue that failed to close.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Record Close Failure Details Error Description, Condition Code, Reason Code, Queue Name

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has attempted to close the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue
acceptance_criteria.When: The queue closure operation fails and returns a non-successful condition code
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program must record the failure condition code, the failure reason code, the queue name CARD.DEMO.ERROR, and set the error description to 'MQCLOSE ERR' to fully document the closure failure

rules.rule_name: Send Error Notification on Error Queue Closure Failure
rules.rule_description: When the error queue fails to close, the program must send an error notification containing the failure details to the error queue so that the failure is captured for monitoring and alerting purposes.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Send Error Notification Write failure details to Error Queue

acceptance_criteria.Given: The error queue closure has failed and the failure details including condition code, reason code, queue name CARD.DEMO.ERROR, and error description 'MQCLOSE ERR' have been recorded
acceptance_criteria.When: The program attempts to notify about the closure failure
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program must invoke the error notification process (9000-ERROR) which writes the full error details to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue, ensuring the failure is logged for operational monitoring

rules.rule_name: Proceed to Program Termination After Error Queue Closure Failure
rules.rule_description: After sending the error notification for the error queue closure failure, the program must proceed to orderly program termination to ensure all remaining resources are released.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Proceed to Program Termination

acceptance_criteria.Given: The error queue closure has failed and the error notification has been sent
acceptance_criteria.When: The error notification process completes
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program must invoke the termination process (8000-TERMINATION) to close any remaining open queues and return control to CICS, ensuring an orderly shutdown regardless of the error queue closure failure

rules.rule_name: Conditional Closure of Input Queue at Program Termination
rules.rule_description: During program termination, the system must check whether the input queue is currently open before attempting to close it, to ensure only active queue connections are released.

acceptance_criteria.Then: If the Input Queue is open, the system proceeds to close it; if it is already closed or was never opened, the system skips the closure step and moves on to check the Output/Reply Queue

rules.rule_name: Close Input Queue During Program Termination
rules.rule_description: When the input queue is confirmed to be open at termination time, the system must formally release the connection to the input queue to free up resources and ensure clean shutdown.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Close Input Queue CARD.DEMO INPUT QUEUE

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program termination sequence is in progress and the Input Queue has been confirmed as currently open
acceptance_criteria.When: The system closes the Input Queue using the stored queue handle
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Input Queue connection is released successfully and the system proceeds to check whether the Output/Reply Queue needs to be closed

rules.rule_name: Conditional Closure of Output/Reply Queue at Program Termination
rules.rule_description: During program termination, the system must check whether the Output/Reply Queue (CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE) is currently open before attempting to close it, ensuring only active connections are released.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Output/Reply Queue Currently Open?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program termination sequence is in progress and the Input Queue check has been completed
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the Output/Reply Queue (CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE) is currently open
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the Output/Reply Queue is open, the system proceeds to close it; if it is already closed or was never opened, the system skips the closure step and moves on to check the Error Queue

rules.rule_name: Close Output/Reply Queue During Program Termination
rules.rule_description: When the Output/Reply Queue (CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE) is confirmed to be open at termination time, the system must formally release the connection to ensure clean shutdown and no orphaned queue connections remain.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Close Output/Reply Queue CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program termination sequence is in progress and the Output/Reply Queue (CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE) has been confirmed as currently open
acceptance_criteria.When: The system closes the Output/Reply Queue (CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE) using the stored output queue handle
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Output/Reply Queue connection is released successfully and the system proceeds to check whether the Error Queue needs to be closed

rules.rule_name: Conditional Closure of Error Queue at Program Termination
rules.rule_description: During program termination, the system must check whether the Error Queue (CARD.DEMO.ERROR) is currently open before attempting to close it, ensuring only active connections are released.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Error Queue Currently Open?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program termination sequence is in progress and the Output/Reply Queue check has been completed
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the Error Queue (CARD.DEMO.ERROR) is currently open
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the Error Queue is open, the system proceeds to close it; if it is already closed or was never opened, the system skips the closure step and proceeds directly to return control to CICS

rules.rule_name: Close Error Queue During Program Termination
rules.rule_description: When the Error Queue (CARD.DEMO.ERROR) is confirmed to be open at termination time, the system must formally release the connection to the error queue to ensure a clean and complete shutdown.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Close Error Queue CARD.DEMO.ERROR

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program termination sequence is in progress and the Error Queue (CARD.DEMO.ERROR) has been confirmed as currently open
acceptance_criteria.When: The system closes the Error Queue (CARD.DEMO.ERROR) using the stored error queue handle
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Error Queue connection is released successfully and the system proceeds to return control to CICS

rules.rule_name: Return Control to CICS to End the Transaction
rules.rule_description: After all open queues have been closed, the program must formally return control to CICS, ending the current transaction and completing the program lifecycle.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Return Control to CICS Transaction Ends

acceptance_criteria.Given: All open queues (Input, Output/Reply, and Error) have been evaluated and closed as applicable during the termination sequence
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the final step of the termination process
acceptance_criteria.Then: Control is returned to CICS, the current transaction is ended, and the program terminates completely

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has been triggered and is starting execution
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program begins its initialization phase
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The input queue name, queue manager name, queue message buffer, and MQ error display area must all be cleared to spaces before any queue operations are attempted

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize Program Working Areas
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before any processing begins, all working storage fields including queue names, message buffers, and error display areas must be cleared to ensure no residual data affects processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has completed initialization of working storage fields
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program attempts to open the error queue named CARD.DEMO.ERROR for output
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the queue opens successfully, the error queue handle is saved and the error queue is marked as open for use throughout the program; if the queue fails to open, the error details are displayed and the program terminates immediately without processing any messages

all_rules.Rule_Name: Open Error Queue Before All Other Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: The error queue CARD.DEMO.ERROR must be opened for writing as the very first queue operation, before any other queues are opened, so that all subsequent errors can be captured and reported.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The error queue has been successfully opened and the program is ready to begin message processing
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program retrieves the CICS trigger message into the MQTM trigger message structure
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The trigger message is retrieved and the program evaluates whether the retrieval was successful before proceeding to extract the input queue name

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve MQ Trigger Message to Determine Input Queue
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program is activated by an MQ trigger mechanism. It must retrieve the CICS trigger message to dynamically determine which input queue contains the date request messages to be processed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has attempted to retrieve the CICS trigger message
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The CICS response code is evaluated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the response is NORMAL, the program extracts the input queue name from the trigger message field MQTM-QNAME and sets the reply queue to CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE; if the response is not NORMAL, the program records the error paragraph as 'CICS RETRIEVE', formats the response codes into an error message string, sends the error to the error queue, and terminates immediately

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Trigger Message Retrieval Success
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program must validate that the CICS trigger message was successfully retrieved before attempting to extract queue names and process messages. If retrieval fails, an error must be reported and processing must stop.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The CICS trigger message has been successfully retrieved
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program extracts queue name information from the trigger message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The input queue name must be set to the value of MQTM-QNAME from the trigger message, and the reply queue name must always be set to the hardcoded value 'CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE'

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Input and Reply Queue Names from Trigger
all_rules.Rule_Description: Upon successful trigger retrieval, the input queue name is dynamically assigned from the trigger message, while the reply queue is always fixed to CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE regardless of the request source.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The input queue name has been set from the trigger message
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program attempts to open the input queue for shared reading
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the queue opens successfully, the input queue handle is saved and the input queue is marked as open; if the queue fails to open, the queue name and error 'INP MQOPEN ERR' are recorded, the error is sent to the error queue, and the program terminates

all_rules.Rule_Name: Open Input Queue for Reading Date Requests
all_rules.Rule_Description: The dynamically determined input queue must be opened for shared reading to allow multiple consumers to access it simultaneously, enabling the program to retrieve incoming date request messages.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The input queue has been successfully opened and the reply queue name is set to CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program attempts to open the reply queue for output
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the queue opens successfully, the output queue handle is saved and the reply queue is marked as open; if the queue fails to open, the queue name and error 'OUT MQOPEN ERR' are recorded, the error is sent to the error queue, and the program terminates

all_rules.Rule_Name: Open Output Reply Queue for Writing Date Responses
all_rules.Rule_Description: The fixed reply queue CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE must be opened for writing before any date/time responses can be sent back to requesting applications.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The input queue is open and the program is ready to retrieve messages
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program attempts to read the next message from the input queue
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must wait up to 5000 milliseconds (5 seconds) for a message; the message buffer size is set to 1000 bytes; message ID and correlation ID filters are cleared so any available message is retrieved; if a message is retrieved it is made available for processing; if no message arrives within 5 seconds the no-more-messages condition is set

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Next Date Request Message with Wait
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program retrieves the next available date request message from the input queue, waiting up to 5 seconds for a message to arrive before concluding that no more messages are available.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has attempted to retrieve a message from the input queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The result of the message retrieval is evaluated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If a message is available, the program saves the message identifiers and proceeds to retrieve the current date and time; if no more messages are available, the program proceeds directly to close the input queue and begin orderly termination

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine Whether More Messages Exist for Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: After each message retrieval attempt, the program must determine whether a message was successfully obtained to decide whether to continue processing or proceed to orderly shutdown.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A date request message has been successfully retrieved from the input queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program processes the incoming message header
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The message ID (MQMD-MSGID) must be saved to SAVE-MSGID and the correlation ID (MQMD-CORRELID) must be saved to SAVE-CORELID so they can be used when sending the reply message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save Message Identifiers for Reply Correlation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a request message is received, its message ID and correlation ID must be saved so that the reply can be correlated back to the original request by the calling application.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A date request message has been received and message identifiers have been saved
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program requests the current system timestamp
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current absolute system time must be retrieved into WS-ABS-TIME for subsequent formatting into human-readable date and time values

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Current System Date and Time
all_rules.Rule_Description: For each date request message received, the program must obtain the current system date and time as the source data for constructing the date/time reply.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current system absolute time has been retrieved into WS-ABS-TIME
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program formats the timestamp
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The date must be formatted as MM-DD-YYYY using a dash ('-') as the date separator and stored in WS-MMDDYYYY; the time must be formatted with time separators and stored in WS-TIME

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format System Date and Time into Readable Format
all_rules.Rule_Description: The raw system timestamp must be formatted into a standardized human-readable date format of MM-DD-YYYY with a dash separator and a time format with time separators before being included in the reply message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system date has been formatted as MM-DD-YYYY in WS-MMDDYYYY and the system time has been formatted in WS-TIME
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program constructs the reply message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The reply message must be built by concatenating the literal 'SYSTEM DATE : ' followed by WS-MMDDYYYY, then the literal 'SYSTEM TIME : ' followed by WS-TIME, all delimited by size, and stored in REPLY-MESSAGE

all_rules.Rule_Name: Construct Date and Time Reply Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: The formatted date and time values must be combined into a standardized reply message string that clearly labels both the system date and system time for the requesting application.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The date/time reply message has been constructed and the original message ID and correlation ID have been saved
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program sends the reply message to the output queue CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The reply message must be placed in a 1000-byte buffer; the saved message ID (SAVE-MSGID) must be set as MQMD-MSGID and the saved correlation ID (SAVE-CORELID) must be set as MQMD-CORRELID on the outgoing message; the message format must be set to string; if the put operation succeeds the condition codes are recorded; if the put operation fails the queue name and error 'MQPUT ERR' are recorded, the error is sent to the error queue, and the program terminates

all_rules.Rule_Name: Send Date/Time Reply Correlated to Original Request
all_rules.Rule_Description: The constructed date/time reply message must be sent to the reply queue with the original request's message identifiers preserved, so the requesting application can match the reply to its original request.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A date request message has been fully processed and its date/time reply has been sent to the reply queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program prepares to retrieve the next message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A CICS SYNCPOINT must be issued to commit the completed message transaction before the next message retrieval attempt, ensuring the reply is permanently written and the processed message is removed from the input queue

all_rules.Rule_Name: Commit Each Message Transaction Before Fetching Next
all_rules.Rule_Description: After each date request message has been processed and its reply sent, the transaction must be committed before retrieving the next message, ensuring each message is processed as an independent, atomic unit of work.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is in active message processing mode with input and output queues open
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program completes processing of one date request message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must loop back to commit the transaction and attempt to retrieve the next message, continuing this cycle until the no-more-messages condition is detected, at which point the loop exits and termination begins

all_rules.Rule_Name: Continuous Message Processing Loop
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program must continuously cycle through committing the previous transaction and retrieving the next message until no more messages are available in the input queue.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A processing error has occurred, including the error paragraph name, queue name, and error condition codes captured in the MQ error display area
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program attempts to write the error notification to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The complete error display information must be moved to the error message buffer and placed onto the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue in a 1000-byte string-formatted message; if the error queue write itself fails, the error details are displayed to the system console and the program terminates immediately

all_rules.Rule_Name: Send Error Notification to Error Queue
all_rules.Rule_Description: When any processing error occurs, the full error details must be written to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue to enable monitoring and alerting of failed operations.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is in the termination phase
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program checks whether the input queue was opened
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the input queue is marked as open, the program must close it using the saved input queue handle; if the close operation fails, the error 'MQCLOSE ERR' is recorded and the program proceeds to termination

all_rules.Rule_Name: Close Input Queue During Termination
all_rules.Rule_Description: During program termination, the input queue must be closed only if it was previously successfully opened, ensuring proper release of queue resources.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The input queue has been closed and the program continues termination
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program checks whether the output reply queue was opened
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the reply queue is marked as open, the program must close it using the saved output queue handle; if the close operation fails, the error 'MQCLOSE ERR' is recorded and the program proceeds to termination

all_rules.Rule_Name: Close Output Reply Queue During Termination
all_rules.Rule_Description: During program termination, the output reply queue must be closed only if it was previously successfully opened, ensuring proper release of queue resources.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The input and output queues have been closed and the program continues termination
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program checks whether the error queue was opened
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the error queue is marked as open, the program must close it using the saved error queue handle; if the close operation fails, the error 'MQCLOSE ERR' is recorded, a final error notification is sent, and the program proceeds to termination

all_rules.Rule_Name: Close Error Queue During Termination
all_rules.Rule_Description: During program termination, the error queue must be closed only if it was previously successfully opened, ensuring all queue resources are properly released before returning control to CICS.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All open queues have been closed during the termination phase
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program has completed all cleanup activities
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must issue a CICS RETURN command to formally end the CICS transaction and return control to the CICS transaction manager

all_rules.Rule_Name: Return Control to CICS on Program Completion
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all queues have been closed, the program must formally return control to CICS to end the transaction, whether the termination was due to normal completion or an error condition.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has just started execution and no queue connections have been established yet
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initializes its working storage fields at the start of a new processing cycle
