Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Input Queue Name field must be set to spaces (blank), ensuring no previously held or residual queue name value is present before the queue name is dynamically assigned from the trigger message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Input Queue Name Before Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before any message processing begins, the input queue name must be cleared to spaces to ensure no residual or stale queue name from a previous execution is carried forward.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has just started execution and no queue manager connections have been established yet
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initializes its working storage fields at the start of a new processing cycle
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Queue Manager Name field must be set to spaces (blank), ensuring the queue manager name is clean and free of any residual value before processing begins

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Queue Manager Name Before Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before any message processing begins, the Queue Manager Name must be cleared to spaces to ensure no stale or inherited value from a prior execution affects the current processing session.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has just started execution and no messages have been retrieved yet
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initializes its working storage fields at the start of a new processing cycle
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Queue Message buffer field must be set to spaces (blank), ensuring the message buffer contains no residual data before new messages are retrieved and processed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Message Buffer Before Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before any message processing begins, the message buffer (QUEUE-MESSAGE) must be cleared to spaces to ensure no leftover message content from a prior execution is present when the program starts reading new messages.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has just started execution and no errors have been encountered yet
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initializes its working storage fields at the start of a new processing cycle
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Error Display Area (MQ-ERR-DISPLAY) must be initialized to its default values (numeric fields reset to zeroes, alphanumeric fields reset to spaces), ensuring all error tracking fields are clean before any error conditions can be encountered during processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize Error Display Area Before Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before any message processing begins, the error display area (MQ-ERR-DISPLAY) must be reset to its default values to ensure any error information captured and reported during this execution session is fresh and not contaminated by data from a previous run.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has started and is preparing to open the error reporting channel
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The error queue is being initialized at the start of the program
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error queue name must be set to 'CARD.DEMO.ERROR' as the designated error message destination

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Dedicated Error Queue Name
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program must use a fixed, designated queue named CARD.DEMO.ERROR as the sole destination for all error messages generated during processing. This queue name is a system-wide constant and is assigned before any queue access is attempted.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The error queue name has been set to 'CARD.DEMO.ERROR' and the program is ready to establish queue access
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program requests write access to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must attempt to open the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue with output (write) permissions so that error messages can be sent to it during processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Request Access to Error Queue for Writing Error Messages
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program must establish write access to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue before any business processing begins. The queue must be opened with output capability, allowing the program to write error messages to it throughout the processing lifecycle.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has requested write access to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The queue is opened successfully without any errors
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must save the active connection reference to the error queue and mark the error queue status as 'Open and Ready', enabling error message delivery for the remainder of the program's execution

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Error Queue as Open and Ready Upon Successful Access
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue is successfully opened for writing, the program must record the queue's active connection handle and flag the error queue as available. This readiness flag is used throughout the program to determine whether error messages can be dispatched and whether the queue needs to be closed during termination.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has requested write access to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The queue cannot be opened due to any failure condition
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must record the name of the queue that failed to open ('CARD.DEMO.ERROR') along with the failure description ('ERR MQOPEN ERR') and all associated error details to the system log, and then immediately terminate all processing without proceeding to any further business operations

all_rules.Rule_Name: Terminate Program When Error Queue Cannot Be Opened
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the program is unable to open the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue for writing, it cannot safely handle any subsequent errors that may arise during processing. In this case, the program must log the failure details to the system and immediately terminate, as continuing without an error reporting channel would leave any future errors undetected and unreported.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has been started by a CICS transaction trigger event and the error queue CARD.DEMO.ERROR has been successfully opened
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program requests the MQ trigger message from the CICS transaction start data
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The trigger message content (MQTM) is retrieved and made available for extraction of the input queue name, along with response indicators that confirm whether the retrieval was successful or not

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve MQ Trigger Message from CICS Transaction Start Data
all_rules.Rule_Description: When this program is initiated by a CICS transaction trigger, it must retrieve the trigger message that contains the identity of the input queue to be processed. This trigger message is the entry point that drives all subsequent processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has submitted a request to retrieve the MQ trigger message from CICS transaction start data
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The CICS response code is evaluated after the retrieval attempt
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the response code indicates a Normal (successful) completion, the program proceeds to extract the input queue name from the trigger message; otherwise, the program treats the retrieval as a failure and initiates error handling

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Successful Retrieval of Trigger Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: After requesting the trigger message from CICS, the program must verify that the retrieval completed successfully before attempting to extract any queue information. Only a normal response code confirms a valid trigger message was received.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The MQ trigger message has been successfully retrieved from CICS transaction start data
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The CICS response code confirms a normal successful retrieval
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The input queue name is extracted from the trigger message queue name field (MQTM-QNAME) and stored as the active Input Queue Name to be used for all subsequent message retrieval operations in this program execution

all_rules.Rule_Name: Extract Input Queue Name from Trigger Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: Upon successful retrieval of the trigger message, the program extracts the name of the input queue that initiated this transaction. This queue name is dynamic and varies per trigger event, determining which queue the program will read messages from during this execution.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The input queue name has been successfully extracted from the trigger message
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program sets up the reply destination for processed responses
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The reply queue name is unconditionally set to the fixed value 'CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE', which will be used as the destination for all date and time reply messages produced during this program execution, regardless of the originating input queue

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Fixed Reply Queue for Date-Time Responses
all_rules.Rule_Description: Regardless of which input queue triggered the program, all date and time response messages must always be directed to a single, fixed reply queue named CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE. This is a mandatory business routing rule that cannot be overridden by the trigger message content.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has attempted to retrieve the MQ trigger message from CICS transaction start data
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The CICS response code indicates an unexpected or unsuccessful response (not a Normal response)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program records the failure by: (1) identifying the failed operation as 'CICS RETRIEVE', (2) capturing the primary CICS response code, (3) capturing the secondary CICS response code, and (4) constructing a combined error message containing the label 'RESP: ' followed by both response code values, to be used in the error notification

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record Trigger Message Retrieval Failure Details
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the trigger message cannot be successfully retrieved from CICS, the program must capture and record the full details of the failure, including the source operation that failed and both response codes, so that the error can be fully diagnosed and reported.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The trigger message retrieval has failed and the failure details including the operation name 'CICS RETRIEVE' and both response codes have been recorded in the error message
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program invokes the error notification process followed by the termination process
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The complete error details are sent as a message to the error queue CARD.DEMO.ERROR, and the program immediately terminates by closing all open queues (input queue if open, output reply queue if open, error queue if open) and returning control to CICS — no further message processing occurs

all_rules.Rule_Name: Send Trigger Retrieval Error Notification and Terminate
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the trigger message retrieval fails, the program must send a full error notification to the designated error queue so that operations teams are alerted, and then immediately terminate all processing since no valid input queue name is available to continue.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has successfully retrieved the CICS trigger message and the trigger message contains a valid queue name in its queue name field (MQTM-QNAME)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The trigger message retrieval completes without error
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The input queue name is set to the queue name value extracted from the trigger message (MQTM-QNAME), which will be used as the source queue for reading incoming date/time request messages

all_rules.Rule_Name: Extract Input Queue Name from Trigger Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the program successfully retrieves the trigger message, it extracts the target input queue name from the trigger message payload and assigns it as the queue from which incoming requests will be read.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has successfully retrieved the CICS trigger message and the input queue name has been extracted from the trigger message
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The queue names are being configured for the processing session
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The reply queue name is unconditionally set to the fixed value 'CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE', meaning all response messages for this program will always be routed to this single destination queue, irrespective of the input queue name received in the trigger message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Fixed Reply Queue Name for Date/Time Responses
all_rules.Rule_Description: Regardless of which input queue the trigger message specifies, the program always directs all date/time response messages to a single, fixed, predefined reply queue named CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has successfully retrieved the trigger message and extracted the input queue name (INPUT-QUEUE-NAME) from the trigger message field MQTM-QNAME
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program prepares to open the input queue for reading incoming date request messages
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The queue manager name field (MQOD-OBJECTQMGRNAME) is cleared to spaces and the dynamically retrieved INPUT-QUEUE-NAME is assigned as the target object name (MQOD-OBJECTNAME) for the open request

all_rules.Rule_Name: Prepare Input Queue Using Trigger-Provided Queue Name
all_rules.Rule_Description: The input queue name is not hardcoded but is dynamically sourced from the trigger message retrieved at program startup. Before requesting access, the queue manager name is cleared and the trigger-provided queue name is assigned as the target input queue.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The input queue name (INPUT-QUEUE-NAME) has been set as the target queue and the queue manager name has been cleared
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program requests access to open the input queue
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The queue must be opened with the following combined access permissions: shared input reading (allowing multiple readers), save-all-context (preserving full message context for correlation), and fail-if-quiescing (preventing reads during queue manager shutdown)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Request Shared Read Access to Input Queue
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program requests access to the input queue with specific access permissions: shared input reading, full message context preservation, and protection against queue manager shutdown. These permissions define how the program interacts with incoming date request messages.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has requested access to the input queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The input queue is opened successfully (condition code equals MQCC-OK)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The returned queue handle (MQ-HOBJ) is saved as INPUT-QUEUE-HANDLE for use in subsequent message read operations, the condition code and reason code are recorded, and the input queue status flag (REPLY-QUEUE-OPEN) is set to TRUE to indicate the queue is open and available for reading

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Input Queue as Ready When Successfully Opened
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the input queue is successfully opened, the program records the queue handle for subsequent message retrieval operations and marks the input queue status as open and available, enabling the rest of the program to proceed with reading date request messages.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has requested access to the input queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The input queue fails to open (condition code is anything other than MQCC-OK)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The condition code and reason code from the failed open attempt are recorded, the INPUT-QUEUE-NAME is captured in the error queue name field (MQ-APPL-QUEUE-NAME), and the error description 'INP MQOPEN ERR' is recorded in the error return message field (MQ-APPL-RETURN-MESSAGE)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Error Details When Input Queue Cannot Be Opened
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the input queue cannot be opened for any reason, the program captures the full error context including the queue name that failed and a descriptive error message, so that the failure can be reported and investigated.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The input queue has failed to open and error details (queue name 'INPUT-QUEUE-NAME' and error description 'INP MQOPEN ERR') have been recorded
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program handles the input queue open failure
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error details are written to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue by invoking the error notification process (9000-ERROR), which places the full error display information into the error queue as a 1000-byte message with string format

all_rules.Rule_Name: Send Error Notification to Error Queue When Input Queue Unavailable
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the input queue cannot be opened, the captured error details are sent to the designated error queue (CARD.DEMO.ERROR) so that operations teams are notified of the failure to access the date request input queue.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The input queue has failed to open, error details have been recorded, and the error notification has been sent to CARD.DEMO.ERROR
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program proceeds to termination after an input queue open failure
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The termination process (8000-TERMINATION) is invoked, which closes the error queue (CARD.DEMO.ERROR) if it was previously opened, and then returns control to CICS, ending the program without processing any date request messages

all_rules.Rule_Name: Terminate Program After Input Queue Open Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the input queue cannot be opened, the program cannot fulfill its purpose of processing date request messages. Therefore, after sending the error notification, the program must close any queues that were already opened and terminate, preventing any partial or incomplete processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has successfully retrieved the trigger message and identified the input queue to process
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program prepares to open the output channel for sending date/time responses
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The reply queue destination must always be set to 'CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE' — this value is fixed and cannot be overridden by any runtime input or trigger message content

all_rules.Rule_Name: Designate Fixed Reply Queue for Date/Time Responses
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program always uses a fixed, hardcoded reply queue named CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE as the destination for all date/time response messages, regardless of the input queue or requestor identity.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The reply queue name has been set to 'CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE' and the error queue is already open
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program attempts to open the reply queue for writing date/time responses
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The queue must be opened in output (write) mode with full message context passing enabled, so that response messages carry the complete originating context of the request

all_rules.Rule_Name: Open Reply Queue for Writing Date/Time Response Messages
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program must open the reply queue CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE in write/output mode so that formatted date and time response messages can be delivered to requestors.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has attempted to open the reply queue 'CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE' for writing
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The queue is opened successfully without any errors
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The reply queue handle must be saved for use in subsequent message write operations, and the reply queue status must be flagged as 'open and ready' so that the program can proceed to retrieve and process incoming requests

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Reply Queue as Ready When Successfully Opened
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the reply queue CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE is successfully opened, the program records the queue handle and marks the reply queue as available, enabling subsequent date/time response messages to be written.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has attempted to open the reply queue 'CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE' for writing date/time responses
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The queue open operation fails for any reason
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must record the error condition code, the error reason code, the name of the queue that failed ('CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE'), and set the error description to 'OUT MQOPEN ERR' to identify this as an output queue open failure

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Error Details When Reply Queue Cannot Be Opened
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the reply queue CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE cannot be opened, the program must capture the failure details including the error condition code, reason code, the queue name that failed, and a descriptive error message to support diagnosis.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The reply queue 'CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE' has failed to open and error details (error code, reason code, queue name, error description 'OUT MQOPEN ERR') have been captured
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program processes the queue open failure
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The full error details must be sent as a message to the error queue 'CARD.DEMO.ERROR' to notify operations of the reply queue open failure before the program terminates

all_rules.Rule_Name: Send Error Notification to Error Queue on Reply Queue Open Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the reply queue CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE cannot be opened, the program must route the captured error details to the designated error queue (CARD.DEMO.ERROR) so that operations teams are notified of the failure.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The reply queue 'CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE' has failed to open and the error notification has been sent to the error queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program completes error notification for the reply queue open failure
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must immediately stop all processing, close any queues that were successfully opened prior to this failure (including the input queue and error queue), and return control — no date/time request messages will be processed during this execution

all_rules.Rule_Name: Terminate Program When Reply Queue Cannot Be Opened
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the reply queue CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE cannot be opened, the program cannot deliver any date/time responses and must perform an orderly termination after sending the error notification, closing all previously opened queues.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is about to attempt reading the next request message from the input queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program prepares to issue a read request against the input queue
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A wait interval of 5000 milliseconds (5 seconds) must be set so that the program waits up to 5 seconds for a message to become available before timing out

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Message Wait Interval Before Reading Input Queue
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before attempting to read a message from the input queue, the program must configure a maximum wait duration of 5 seconds. If no message arrives within this window, the program stops waiting and proceeds accordingly.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is preparing to read a message from the designated input queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The read operation is being configured
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The message buffer length must be set to 1000 bytes to accommodate the incoming request message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Message Buffer Size for Input Queue Read
all_rules.Rule_Description: When preparing to read a request message from the input queue, the program must allocate a fixed 1000-byte buffer to receive the message content.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is preparing to read the next available message from the input queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The message read parameters are being initialized
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Both the Message ID and the Correlation ID must be cleared to their default empty values (MQMI-NONE and MQCI-NONE respectively) so that the queue manager retrieves the next available message without filtering by any specific identifier

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Message Identifiers Before Reading New Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before reading a new message from the input queue, the program must reset the Message ID and Correlation ID to blank/none values to ensure no stale identifiers from a previous message influence the retrieval of the next message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The input queue has been successfully opened, the wait interval is set to 5 seconds, the buffer is set to 1000 bytes, and Message ID and Correlation ID have been cleared
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program issues a read request against the input queue identified by INPUT-QUEUE-NAME using the input queue handle
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program retrieves the next available message from the input queue and the outcome (message received, no more messages, or error) is captured for subsequent decision processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Read Next Available Request Message from Input Queue
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program must attempt to retrieve the next available request message from the designated input queue using the configured wait interval and buffer settings.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A request message has been successfully retrieved from the input queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The message retrieval operation completes with a successful result
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Message ID (MQMD-MSGID) must be saved into SAVE-MSGID and the Correlation ID (MQMD-CORRELID) must be saved into SAVE-CORELID so they can be used when sending the reply message back to the requester

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save Message Identifiers Upon Successful Message Retrieval
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a message is successfully retrieved from the input queue, the program must capture and preserve the Message ID and Correlation ID from the incoming message. These identifiers are required later to correctly correlate the reply message back to the original request.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A request message has been successfully retrieved from the input queue and the Message ID and Correlation ID have been saved
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The message details have been captured
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must proceed to the date and time processing step (4000-PROCESS-REQUEST-REPLY) to generate the system date and time response for the requester

all_rules.Rule_Name: Proceed to Date/Time Processing After Message Retrieval
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once a request message has been successfully retrieved and its identifiers saved, the program must immediately proceed to generate and return the current system date and time as the response.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has issued a read request against the input queue and the 5-second wait interval has expired
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The queue returns a 'no more messages' condition (reason code MQRC-NO-MSG-AVAILABLE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The NO-MORE-MSGS flag must be set to TRUE, which causes the message processing loop to exit and the program to proceed to the termination and queue-closing steps

all_rules.Rule_Name: End Message Processing When No More Messages Are Available
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the input queue has no more messages available after the 5-second wait interval expires, the program must recognize this as the normal end-of-processing condition and stop the message processing loop.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has issued a read request against the input queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The read operation returns an unexpected error condition (neither a successful message retrieval nor a no-more-messages condition)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must capture the error condition code and reason code, record the input queue name as the source of the error, set the error message to identify the failure, send the full error details to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR error queue via the 9000-ERROR routine, and then proceed to the termination step (8000-TERMINATION) to close all open queues and end processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Send Error Notification on Unexpected Message Retrieval Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: If an unexpected error occurs while attempting to read a message from the input queue (any condition other than successful retrieval or no-more-messages), the program must log the error details to the error queue and terminate processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A request message has been successfully retrieved from the input queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program prepares to send a reply to the requester
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The original Message ID (SAVE-MSGID) from the incoming request must be copied into the reply message descriptor (MQMD-MSGID), ensuring the reply carries the same Message ID as the original request for traceability

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save Incoming Message ID for Reply Correlation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a request message is successfully retrieved from the input queue, the program must capture and preserve the original message's unique identifier so that the reply can be linked back to the originating request.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A request message has been successfully retrieved from the input queue and its Message ID has been saved
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program prepares to send a reply to the requester
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The original Correlation ID (SAVE-CORELID) from the incoming request must be copied into the reply message descriptor (MQMD-CORRELID), ensuring the reply is traceable to the originating transaction or conversation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save Incoming Correlation ID for Reply Tracking
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a request message is successfully retrieved from the input queue, the program must capture and preserve the original message's correlation identifier so that the reply can be matched to the correct conversation or transaction chain by the requesting application.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has successfully retrieved the CICS trigger message
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program sets up the reply routing destination
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The reply queue name must always be set to 'CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE' as a fixed, hardcoded destination for all date and time response messages, and this queue must be opened for output before any message processing begins

all_rules.Rule_Name: Fixed Reply-To Queue Assignment for Date-Time Responses
all_rules.Rule_Description: The destination queue for all date and time responses is always fixed to CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE, regardless of the content of the incoming request message. This queue name is assigned at program startup when the trigger message is received and does not vary per message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A request message has been retrieved from the input queue and the system date and time have been formatted into the reply message
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program is ready to send the reply
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The reply message must be sent to the output queue (CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE) only when all three identifiers are set: the Message ID (SAVE-MSGID copied to MQMD-MSGID), the Correlation ID (SAVE-CORELID copied to MQMD-CORRELID), and the reply destination queue (OUTPUT-QUEUE-HANDLE referencing CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE); if any identifier is missing or the PUT operation fails, an error must be reported to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue and processing must terminate

all_rules.Rule_Name: All Message Identifiers Must Be Present Before Reply Is Sent
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before a date and time reply message can be dispatched, all three required identifiers — Message ID, Correlation ID, and Reply-To Queue — must be available and populated. These identifiers together ensure the reply is correctly routed and correlated to the original request.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has attempted to send a reply message with the saved Message ID, Correlation ID, and reply queue destination
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The message PUT operation to the reply queue (CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE) does not complete successfully
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must capture the error details including the queue name (REPLY-QUEUE-NAME) and the error description ('MQPUT ERR'), send the full error information to the error queue (CARD.DEMO.ERROR), and immediately terminate all processing by closing all open queues and returning control

all_rules.Rule_Name: Report Error and End Processing When Identifier Saving Fails
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the reply message cannot be successfully placed onto the reply queue — indicating that message identifiers or routing information could not be applied correctly — the failure details must be reported to the error queue and all processing must stop.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A request message has been retrieved from the input queue and the reply message area and date-time working storage have been cleared and initialized to zeroes
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system requests the current absolute timestamp from CICS (ASKTIME)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current absolute system timestamp is captured and stored in the working storage field WS-ABS-TIME, making it available for subsequent date and time formatting

all_rules.Rule_Name: Request Current System Timestamp
all_rules.Rule_Description: When processing a date/time request message, the system must obtain the current absolute system timestamp from CICS before any date or time formatting can occur.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The date-time working storage area has been initialized to zeroes and the system is ready to capture the current timestamp
Acceptance_Criteria.When: CICS ASKTIME returns the current absolute system time
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The absolute timestamp value is stored in WS-ABS-TIME and held in working storage, ensuring it is available as the single source of truth for both date formatting (MM-DD-YYYY) and time formatting in the subsequent formatting step

all_rules.Rule_Name: Store Absolute Timestamp for Formatting
all_rules.Rule_Description: The raw absolute timestamp obtained from CICS must be retained in a dedicated working storage area so it can be used as the source value for formatting into human-readable date and time representations.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The absolute timestamp has been successfully captured and stored in WS-ABS-TIME
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system formats the absolute timestamp using CICS FORMATTIME
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The date is formatted as MM-DD-YYYY with a dash ('-') as the date separator and stored in WS-MMDDYYYY, and the time is formatted with a time separator and stored in WS-TIME, after which the reply message is constructed as 'SYSTEM DATE : MM-DD-YYYY SYSTEM TIME : HH:MM:SS' and placed into the REPLY-MESSAGE field ready to be sent to the CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE queue

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format Absolute Timestamp into Date and Time
all_rules.Rule_Description: The stored absolute timestamp must be converted into a human-readable date in MM-DD-YYYY format with dash separators and a time value with time separators, so that a meaningful date and time response message can be constructed for the requester.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A new request message has been retrieved from the input queue and is ready for processing
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system begins preparing a date/time reply for the requesting application
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The reply message buffer (REPLY-MESSAGE) must be cleared to spaces, and all date/time working fields (WS-DATE-TIME) must be reset to zeroes before any date or time values are populated

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Reply Buffer and Reset Date/Time Fields Before Formatting
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before constructing a date/time reply message, the reply message buffer and all date/time working fields must be cleared to ensure no residual data from previous processing contaminates the new response.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The reply message buffer and date/time fields have been cleared and initialized
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system needs to determine the current date and time to include in the reply
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must invoke CICS ASKTIME to retrieve the current absolute timestamp (WS-ABS-TIME), which serves as the single source of truth for both the date and time values in the reply

all_rules.Rule_Name: Obtain Current System Absolute Timestamp
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system must capture the current absolute timestamp from the CICS system clock as the authoritative source for the date and time values that will be returned in the reply message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current absolute timestamp (WS-ABS-TIME) has been successfully obtained from the system clock
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system formats the date portion of the timestamp
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The date must be formatted into the MM-DD-YYYY pattern (e.g., 01-15-2025) using a dash ('-') as the date separator, and the result must be stored in WS-MMDDYYYY for inclusion in the reply message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format Date into MM-DD-YYYY Pattern with Dash Separator
all_rules.Rule_Description: The absolute timestamp must be converted into a human-readable date string following the MM-DD-YYYY format, with a dash character used as the separator between month, day, and year components.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current absolute timestamp (WS-ABS-TIME) has been successfully obtained from the system clock
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system formats the time portion of the timestamp
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The time must be formatted into the HH:MM:SS pattern (e.g., 14:30:45) using a colon as the time separator (TIMESEP), and the result must be stored in WS-TIME for inclusion in the reply message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format Time into HH:MM:SS Pattern with Colon Separator
all_rules.Rule_Description: The absolute timestamp must also be converted into a human-readable time string following the HH:MM:SS format, with a colon character used as the separator between hours, minutes, and seconds components.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The date has been formatted as MM-DD-YYYY (e.g., 01-15-2025) and stored in WS-MMDDYYYY, and the time has been formatted as HH:MM:SS (e.g., 14:30:45) and stored in WS-TIME
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system assembles the final reply message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The reply message (REPLY-MESSAGE) must be constructed by concatenating the literal label 'SYSTEM DATE : ' followed by the formatted date (WS-MMDDYYYY), then the literal label 'SYSTEM TIME : ' followed by the formatted time (WS-TIME), all within a 1000-byte reply buffer, and this completed message must then be sent to the reply queue CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE

all_rules.Rule_Name: Construct Reply Message Combining Formatted Date and Time
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once both the date and time have been successfully formatted, they must be combined into a single standardized reply message string that clearly labels both the system date and system time for the requesting application.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A new request message has been retrieved from the input queue and the system is preparing to build a reply
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The reply message construction process begins
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The reply message buffer must be cleared to spaces AND all date and time working fields must be reset to zeroes before any new date or time values are populated

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Reply Message Buffer Before Building New Response
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before constructing a new date/time reply message, the reply message buffer and all date/time working fields must be cleared to ensure no residual data from a previous message contaminates the new response.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The reply message buffer and date/time working fields have been cleared and the system is ready to build the date/time response
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system retrieves the current absolute time and formats the date
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current system date must be formatted as MM-DD-YYYY using a hyphen (-) as the date separator and stored in the date working field (WS-MMDDYYYY) for inclusion in the reply message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Current System Date in MM-DD-YYYY Format
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system must retrieve the current system date and format it in MM-DD-YYYY format with a hyphen (-) as the date separator, to be included in the reply message sent back to the requester.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current system absolute time has been retrieved and the date has been formatted in MM-DD-YYYY format
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system formats the time component from the same absolute time retrieval
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current system time must be formatted with a time separator (colon) producing HH:MM:SS format and stored in the time working field (WS-TIME) for inclusion in the reply message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Current System Time with Time Separator
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system must retrieve the current system time with a time separator applied, to be included alongside the date in the reply message sent back to the requester.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system date has been formatted as MM-DD-YYYY and the system time has been formatted with a time separator
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The reply message string is being constructed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The reply message must begin with the literal label 'SYSTEM DATE : ' immediately followed by the formatted date value in MM-DD-YYYY format, concatenated into the reply message field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Construct Reply Message with Labeled System Date
all_rules.Rule_Description: The formatted system date must be combined with a descriptive label 'SYSTEM DATE :' to form the first part of the reply message, making the date value clearly identifiable to the receiving application.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The reply message already contains the labeled system date ('SYSTEM DATE : MM-DD-YYYY') and the system time has been formatted with a time separator
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The reply message string construction is finalized using a STRING operation delimited by size
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The literal label 'SYSTEM TIME : ' followed by the formatted time value must be appended to the reply message field, resulting in a complete reply message in the format: 'SYSTEM DATE : MM-DD-YYYY SYSTEM TIME : HH:MM:SS', all combined into the REPLY-MESSAGE field in a single STRING operation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Append Labeled System Time to Complete Reply Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: The formatted system time must be appended to the reply message with a descriptive label 'SYSTEM TIME :' immediately following the date portion, completing the full date/time reply message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A date/time reply message has been constructed containing the current system date in MM-DD-YYYY format and current system time
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program prepares to send the reply message to the output queue
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The formatted date/time reply message is loaded into the message buffer, and the message buffer length is set to 1000 bytes for transmission

all_rules.Rule_Name: Load Date/Time Reply Message into Transmission Buffer
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before sending the reply, the formatted date and time message must be loaded into the message buffer with a fixed transmission size of 1000 bytes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The original request message was received and its Message ID and Correlation ID were saved
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The reply message is being prepared for sending
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The saved Message ID from the original request is applied to the reply message descriptor, and the saved Correlation ID from the original request is applied to the reply message descriptor, so the reply is correctly paired with the original request

all_rules.Rule_Name: Correlate Reply Message to Original Request
all_rules.Rule_Description: The reply message must be linked back to the original incoming request by applying the saved Message ID and Correlation ID from the original request, ensuring the requester can match the reply to their original message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The reply message buffer has been populated with the formatted date/time content
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The message descriptor is being configured prior to sending
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The message format is set to text string type and the character set is set to the queue manager's character set, ensuring the receiver can correctly read the date/time reply

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Reply Message Format as Text String
all_rules.Rule_Description: The reply message must be marked as a text string format and assigned the queue manager's character set to ensure the receiving application can correctly interpret the date/time content.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The reply message buffer is populated, message format is set to text string, correlation identifiers are applied, and the reply queue CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE is open for output
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program writes the reply message to the output queue
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The date/time reply message is placed onto the CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE queue within a syncpoint transaction boundary, making it available to the requesting application

all_rules.Rule_Name: Deliver Reply Message to Reply Queue
all_rules.Rule_Description: The prepared date/time reply message is written to the designated reply queue CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE as part of a synchronized transaction unit, ensuring delivery integrity.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The reply message has been submitted to the CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The queue manager confirms the message was accepted successfully
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The completion condition code and reason code returned by the queue manager are captured and stored as confirmation of successful delivery

all_rules.Rule_Name: Confirm Successful Reply Message Delivery
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the reply message is successfully delivered to the reply queue, the program records the confirmation details for audit and traceability purposes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The reply message was submitted to the CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The queue manager reports that the message delivery was not successful
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The condition code returned by the queue manager is recorded, the reason code returned by the queue manager is recorded, the queue name CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE is recorded as the failing queue, and the error description 'MQPUT ERR' is recorded to identify the nature of the failure

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Reply Delivery Failure Details
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the reply message cannot be delivered to the reply queue, the program captures all relevant failure details including the error description, condition code, reason code, and the name of the queue that failed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A reply message delivery failure has occurred and error details including condition code, reason code, queue name, and error description have been captured
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program processes the delivery failure
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The full error details are written to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue within a syncpoint transaction boundary, making the failure visible to operations monitoring; if writing to the error queue also fails, the error details are displayed and the program proceeds to close all queues and terminate

all_rules.Rule_Name: Send Reply Failure Notification to Error Queue
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a reply message delivery failure occurs, the complete error information must be forwarded to the central error queue CARD.DEMO.ERROR so that operations teams are notified of the failure.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A reply message delivery failure has occurred and the error notification has been sent to CARD.DEMO.ERROR
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initiates termination
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The input queue is closed if it was open, the reply queue CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE is closed if it was open, the error queue CARD.DEMO.ERROR is closed if it was open, and the program returns control to the calling system

all_rules.Rule_Name: Terminate Program After Reply Delivery Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: Following a reply message delivery failure and error notification, the program must perform an orderly shutdown by closing all open queues before ending.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The message processing loop is active and at least one message has been previously processed and replied to
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program is about to retrieve the next message from the input queue
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A transaction syncpoint (commit) is issued to permanently secure the previously processed message and its reply before proceeding to retrieve the next message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Commit Transaction Before Processing Next Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before retrieving the next request message from the input queue, the program commits the current unit of work to permanently secure any previously processed message and its reply.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The input queue is open and the program is in the message processing loop
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program attempts to retrieve a message from the input queue
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program waits up to 5000 milliseconds (5 seconds) for a message to become available; the message buffer is set to 1000 bytes; message ID and correlation ID are cleared before each retrieval attempt to ensure a fresh, unfiltered message fetch

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Next Request Message with Wait Timeout
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program attempts to retrieve the next available date request message from the input queue, waiting up to 5 seconds for a message to arrive before concluding no more messages are available.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is waiting for a message from the input queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: No message is received within the 5-second wait interval (wait timeout occurs)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The NO-MORE-MSGS condition is set to TRUE, the message processing loop exits, and the program proceeds to the queue closure and termination phase

all_rules.Rule_Name: Exit Message Loop When No More Messages Available
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the input queue wait interval expires without a message being received, the program exits the message processing loop and proceeds to close all queues and terminate.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A request message has been successfully retrieved from the input queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The message is received and ready for processing
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The original Message ID is saved to SAVE-MSGID and the original Correlation ID is saved to SAVE-CORELID so they can be used when sending the reply, enabling the calling application to match the reply to its original request

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save Request Message Identifiers for Reply Correlation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a request message is successfully retrieved, the program saves the original message's identifiers so that the reply can be correlated back to the original request by the calling application.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A date request message has been received and its identifiers have been saved
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program processes the date request
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current system absolute time (WS-ABS-TIME) is retrieved from the system clock to serve as the basis for formatting the date and time response

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Current System Date and Time
all_rules.Rule_Description: For each date request message received, the program retrieves the current system date and time as the core business data to be returned in the reply.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current system absolute time (WS-ABS-TIME) has been retrieved
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program formats the date and time for the reply message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The date is formatted into WS-MMDDYYYY using MM-DD-YYYY format with a dash ('-') as the date separator, and the time is formatted into WS-TIME using HH:MM:SS format with the default time separator

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format System Date as MM-DD-YYYY and Time as HH:MM:SS
all_rules.Rule_Description: The retrieved system absolute time is formatted into a human-readable date in MM-DD-YYYY format with dash separators, and a time in HH:MM:SS format with time separators.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system date has been formatted as MM-DD-YYYY in WS-MMDDYYYY and the system time has been formatted as HH:MM:SS in WS-TIME
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program constructs the reply message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A reply message is built in REPLY-MESSAGE by concatenating the literal 'SYSTEM DATE : ' followed by the formatted date (WS-MMDDYYYY), then the literal 'SYSTEM TIME : ' followed by the formatted time (WS-TIME), all delimited by size

all_rules.Rule_Name: Build Date and Time Reply Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: The formatted date and time values are combined into a standardized reply message string that will be sent back to the requesting application.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The reply message containing the system date and time has been built in REPLY-MESSAGE
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program sends the reply to the reply queue CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The reply message is placed on the CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE queue with: the reply buffer set to 1000 bytes; the original request's Message ID (SAVE-MSGID) set as MQMD-MSGID; the original request's Correlation ID (SAVE-CORELID) set as MQMD-CORRELID; message format set to string; and the put operation included within the current syncpoint scope

all_rules.Rule_Name: Send Date-Time Reply Correlated to Original Request
all_rules.Rule_Description: The constructed date and time reply message is sent to the fixed reply queue, with the original request's message identifiers preserved to allow the calling application to correlate the reply to its original request.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has attempted to send the date-time reply message to the reply queue CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The result of the message put operation is evaluated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the put operation completed successfully (condition code is MQCC-OK), the program loops back to commit the transaction and retrieve the next message; if the put operation failed (any other condition code), the reply queue name is recorded, a 'MQPUT ERR' error message is generated, an error notification is sent to the error queue, and the program proceeds to terminate

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Successful Reply Message Delivery
all_rules.Rule_Description: After attempting to send the reply message, the program evaluates whether the delivery was successful and determines the next course of action — either continuing to process more messages or handling the delivery failure.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has failed to send the date-time reply message to the reply queue CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The error handling routine is invoked
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The full error display information (MQ-ERR-DISPLAY) is moved to the error message buffer; the error message is placed on the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue with a 1000-byte buffer, string format, and within the current syncpoint scope; if the error queue put also fails, the error details are displayed and the program proceeds directly to termination; after the error notification is sent, the program proceeds to close all queues and terminate

all_rules.Rule_Name: Send Error Notification to Error Queue on Reply Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a reply message cannot be successfully delivered to the reply queue, the program sends a detailed error notification to the designated error queue to alert operations and support teams.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A message has been successfully retrieved from the input queue and its date/time reply has been placed onto the reply queue CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system is ready to process the next message in the input queue
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must issue a transaction commit (SYNCPOINT) to permanently save all changes made for the current message transaction before proceeding to retrieve the next message, ensuring the reply is durably recorded and cannot be rolled back by subsequent processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Commit Processed Message Transaction Before Retrieving Next Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before retrieving the next message from the input queue, the system must permanently save (commit) all changes made during the processing of the current message. This ensures each message's reply is independently and permanently recorded.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction commit (SYNCPOINT) has been issued to permanently save the reply for the current message
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The commit cycle completes and there are more messages to process (NO-MORE-MSGS condition is not set)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must immediately proceed to retrieve the next request message from the input queue, waiting up to 5000 milliseconds for a message to arrive, before repeating the process-and-commit cycle

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Next Request Message After Successful Commit
all_rules.Rule_Description: Only after the transaction commit has been issued for the current message does the system proceed to retrieve the next pending request message from the input queue. This enforces a strict sequence: commit first, then fetch next.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The input queue has been successfully opened and at least one message has been retrieved and processed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The commit-and-retrieve cycle completes for each message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must continue repeating the transaction commit followed by next-message retrieval until the NO-MORE-MSGS condition is reached, at which point the processing loop ends and the program proceeds to orderly termination

all_rules.Rule_Name: Repeat Commit and Retrieve Cycle Until No More Messages Remain
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system continuously repeats the cycle of committing the current transaction and retrieving the next message until the input queue is exhausted (no more messages are available). Each message is treated as an independent unit of work.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An error condition has been detected during queue processing or message handling, and the error details are available including: an error description (e.g., 'INP MQOPEN ERR', 'OUT MQOPEN ERR', 'MQPUT ERR'), a condition code, a reason code, and the name of the queue involved
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The error handling process is triggered by any queue operation failure (open, put, or close)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must collect and store: the error description into MQ-APPL-RETURN-MESSAGE, the condition code into MQ-APPL-CONDITION-CODE, the reason code into MQ-APPL-REASON-CODE, and the queue name into MQ-APPL-QUEUE-NAME; then combine all these details from MQ-ERR-DISPLAY into a single error notification message (ERROR-MESSAGE) ready for dispatch to the error queue

all_rules.Rule_Name: Collect Error Details for Notification
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an error condition is detected during processing, the system collects all relevant error details including the error description, condition code, reason code, and the name of the queue where the error occurred, and consolidates them into a single error notification message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An error notification message has been prepared containing all error details (error description, condition code, reason code, queue name), the error queue CARD.DEMO.ERROR is open and available, and the message buffer is set to 1000 bytes with string format
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to write the error notification message to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue using the MQPUT operation with syncpoint and default context options
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error message must be successfully placed onto the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue; the condition code and reason code from the write operation must be recorded; if the write is successful, control returns to the calling process

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Error Notification to Error Queue
all_rules.Rule_Description: The consolidated error notification message must be written to the designated error queue CARD.DEMO.ERROR so that errors are centrally captured and available for monitoring and alerting.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to write an error notification message to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The MQPUT operation to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue completes and returns a condition code of OK (success)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system records the successful condition code and reason code, and returns control to the calling process that originally triggered the error handling

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle Successful Error Notification Delivery
all_rules.Rule_Description: After attempting to write the error notification to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue, the system evaluates whether the write was successful and records the outcome accordingly.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to write an error notification message to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue, and the MQPUT operation has returned a condition code other than OK (failure)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The write to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue fails for any reason
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: record the failed condition code and reason code, record the error queue name (CARD.DEMO.ERROR) as the queue where the failure occurred, record 'MQPUT ERR' as the error description, display the full error details locally (MQ-ERR-DISPLAY), and immediately initiate program termination by closing all open queues and stopping all processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle Failed Error Notification Delivery
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the system is unable to write the error notification to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue, it must display the error details locally and immediately terminate all processing to prevent further data integrity issues.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is performing a queue operation such as opening the input queue, opening the output queue, or putting a reply message onto a queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Any queue operation returns a condition code other than OK (i.e., the operation did not succeed)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must immediately invoke the error notification process (9000-ERROR) to capture and dispatch the error details to CARD.DEMO.ERROR, followed by invoking the termination process (8000-TERMINATION) to close all open queues and stop processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initiate Error Handling on Queue Operation Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: Whenever a queue operation (opening input queue, opening output queue, or putting a reply message) fails, the system must immediately invoke the error notification process before proceeding to termination.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has completed processing messages or encountered an error requiring termination, and the input queue was previously opened successfully
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program prepares to close the input queue
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The input queue name (dynamically assigned from the trigger message) and its corresponding active queue handle are identified and set as the target for the close operation, with no-options (MQCO-NONE) applied indicating a standard close with no special behavior

all_rules.Rule_Name: Identify Input Queue for Closure
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before closing the input queue, the program identifies the correct queue by associating the input queue name with its active queue handle to ensure the correct queue is targeted for closure.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The input queue name and its active queue handle have been identified, and the queue connection handle is active
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program issues a close request to the messaging system (MQCLOSE) using the queue connection handle, the input queue handle, and standard close options
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The messaging system processes the close request and returns a condition code and reason code indicating the outcome of the closure attempt

all_rules.Rule_Name: Request to Close Input Queue
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program submits a formal request to the messaging system to close the input queue using the established queue connection and handle.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A close request was submitted for the input queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The messaging system returns a successful condition code (MQCC-OK) for the close operation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program records the successful condition code and reason code returned by the messaging system, and control returns to the termination routine to proceed with closing the output/reply queue next

all_rules.Rule_Name: Input Queue Closed Successfully
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the input queue is closed without errors, the program records the successful outcome and proceeds to close the output/reply queue as the next step in the orderly shutdown sequence.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A close request was submitted for the input queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The messaging system returns a condition code other than success (not MQCC-OK) for the close operation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program records the failure condition code, the failure reason code, the input queue name as the queue that failed to close, and sets the return message to 'MQCLOSE ERR' to identify the nature of the failure

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record Input Queue Close Failure Details
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the input queue cannot be closed successfully, the program captures all relevant failure information including the queue name and failure indicators to support error diagnosis and reporting.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The input queue close operation has failed and failure details have been recorded
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program determines it cannot successfully close the input queue
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program immediately invokes the termination routine (8000-TERMINATION), which will attempt to close any remaining open queues (output queue and error queue if still open) and return control to CICS, bypassing the normal sequential close of the output queue

all_rules.Rule_Name: Proceed to Program Termination on Close Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the input queue fails to close, the program bypasses the normal sequential shutdown of remaining queues and immediately invokes the full termination routine to ensure the program ends in a controlled manner.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The input queue has been successfully closed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Control returns to the termination routine after successful input queue closure
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program checks whether the output/reply queue (CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE) is marked as open, and if so, proceeds to close it as the next step in the orderly shutdown sequence

all_rules.Rule_Name: Proceed to Close Output/Reply Queue After Input Queue Closure
all_rules.Rule_Description: After successfully closing the input queue, the program follows the defined shutdown sequence by proceeding to close the output/reply queue as the next step.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The output/reply queue CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE has been previously opened and is currently active
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program reaches its termination phase, either after normal completion of all message processing or after encountering an error condition
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must attempt to close the CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE reply queue using the stored output queue handle to release the queue resource

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initiate Closure of Reply Queue
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the program completes processing or encounters an error, it must attempt to close the reply queue CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE to release the queue resource.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An attempt has been made to close the CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE reply queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The queue close operation returns a successful completion code
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program records the successful condition code and reason code, and the output/reply queue is considered successfully closed with no further action required

all_rules.Rule_Name: Confirm Successful Reply Queue Closure
all_rules.Rule_Description: After attempting to close the reply queue, the program evaluates whether the closure was successful and proceeds accordingly.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An attempt has been made to close the CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE reply queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The queue close operation returns a failure condition code (any condition other than successful completion)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must record the failure condition code, the failure reason code, and the queue name (CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE stored as input queue name) along with the error message 'MQCLOSE ERR' to identify the nature of the closure failure

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Reply Queue Closure Failure Details
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the reply queue closure fails, the program must capture and record all relevant error details including the condition code, reason code, and the name of the queue that failed to close.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The reply queue CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE has failed to close and error details including condition code, reason code, queue name, and error message 'MQCLOSE ERR' have been recorded
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The error details are ready to be reported
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must send the complete error information as a message to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue using the error queue handle, so that the failure is visible for operational monitoring and alerting

all_rules.Rule_Name: Send Reply Queue Closure Error Notification
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the reply queue fails to close, the program must send a full error notification message containing the error details to the designated error queue CARD.DEMO.ERROR for monitoring and alerting purposes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The reply queue CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE has failed to close and the error notification has been sent to CARD.DEMO.ERROR
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The error notification has been successfully dispatched to the error queue
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must immediately invoke the termination routine to perform an orderly shutdown, which includes closing any remaining open queues (input and error queues) and returning control back to the calling system

all_rules.Rule_Name: Proceed to Program Termination After Reply Queue Error
all_rules.Rule_Description: After sending the error notification for a reply queue closure failure, the program must proceed to the termination routine to ensure an orderly shutdown.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has reached its termination phase
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program checks whether the reply queue CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE was successfully opened during initialization
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must only attempt to close the reply queue if it was previously opened (RESP-QUEUE-OPEN flag is set to TRUE); if the queue was never opened, the closure step is skipped entirely

all_rules.Rule_Name: Conditional Execution of Reply Queue Closure
all_rules.Rule_Description: The reply queue closure is only attempted if the reply queue was successfully opened earlier in the program, preventing unnecessary closure attempts on queues that were never opened.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The error queue named CARD.DEMO.ERROR is open and held by the program, and the program has reached the point of termination or completion
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initiates the closure of the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must attempt to close the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue using the stored error queue handle and queue name

all_rules.Rule_Name: Attempt to Close the Error Queue
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the program has completed processing or encountered an error, it must attempt to close the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue to release queue resources before termination.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has attempted to close the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The queue closure operation completes successfully with no errors
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program records the successful condition code and reason code from the close operation, confirming that the error queue resources have been released successfully

all_rules.Rule_Name: Confirm Successful Closure of Error Queue
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the error queue is successfully closed, the program acknowledges the successful release of the queue resource and records the outcome.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has attempted to close the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The queue closure operation fails and returns a non-successful condition code
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must record the failure condition code, the failure reason code, the queue name CARD.DEMO.ERROR, and set the error description to 'MQCLOSE ERR' to fully document the closure failure

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record Error Queue Closure Failure Details
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the error queue cannot be closed successfully, the program must capture and record all relevant failure details including the error description, condition code, reason code, and the name of the queue that failed to close.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The error queue closure has failed and the failure details including condition code, reason code, queue name CARD.DEMO.ERROR, and error description 'MQCLOSE ERR' have been recorded
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program attempts to notify about the closure failure
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must invoke the error notification process (9000-ERROR) which writes the full error details to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue, ensuring the failure is logged for operational monitoring

all_rules.Rule_Name: Send Error Notification on Error Queue Closure Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the error queue fails to close, the program must send an error notification containing the failure details to the error queue so that the failure is captured for monitoring and alerting purposes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The error queue closure has failed and the error notification has been sent
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The error notification process completes
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must invoke the termination process (8000-TERMINATION) to close any remaining open queues and return control to CICS, ensuring an orderly shutdown regardless of the error queue closure failure

all_rules.Rule_Name: Proceed to Program Termination After Error Queue Closure Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: After sending the error notification for the error queue closure failure, the program must proceed to orderly program termination to ensure all remaining resources are released.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program termination sequence has been initiated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the Input Queue (dynamically named from the trigger message) is currently open
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the Input Queue is open, the system proceeds to close it; if it is already closed or was never opened, the system skips the closure step and moves on to check the Output/Reply Queue

all_rules.Rule_Name: Conditional Closure of Input Queue at Program Termination
all_rules.Rule_Description: During program termination, the system must check whether the input queue is currently open before attempting to close it, to ensure only active queue connections are released.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program termination sequence is in progress and the Input Queue has been confirmed as currently open
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system closes the Input Queue using the stored queue handle
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Input Queue connection is released successfully and the system proceeds to check whether the Output/Reply Queue needs to be closed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Close Input Queue During Program Termination
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the input queue is confirmed to be open at termination time, the system must formally release the connection to the input queue to free up resources and ensure clean shutdown.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program termination sequence is in progress and the Input Queue check has been completed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the Output/Reply Queue (CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE) is currently open
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the Output/Reply Queue is open, the system proceeds to close it; if it is already closed or was never opened, the system skips the closure step and moves on to check the Error Queue

all_rules.Rule_Name: Conditional Closure of Output/Reply Queue at Program Termination
all_rules.Rule_Description: During program termination, the system must check whether the Output/Reply Queue (CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE) is currently open before attempting to close it, ensuring only active connections are released.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program termination sequence is in progress and the Output/Reply Queue (CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE) has been confirmed as currently open
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system closes the Output/Reply Queue (CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE) using the stored output queue handle
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Output/Reply Queue connection is released successfully and the system proceeds to check whether the Error Queue needs to be closed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Close Output/Reply Queue During Program Termination
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Output/Reply Queue (CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE) is confirmed to be open at termination time, the system must formally release the connection to ensure clean shutdown and no orphaned queue connections remain.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program termination sequence is in progress and the Output/Reply Queue check has been completed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the Error Queue (CARD.DEMO.ERROR) is currently open
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the Error Queue is open, the system proceeds to close it; if it is already closed or was never opened, the system skips the closure step and proceeds directly to return control to CICS

all_rules.Rule_Name: Conditional Closure of Error Queue at Program Termination
all_rules.Rule_Description: During program termination, the system must check whether the Error Queue (CARD.DEMO.ERROR) is currently open before attempting to close it, ensuring only active connections are released.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program termination sequence is in progress and the Error Queue (CARD.DEMO.ERROR) has been confirmed as currently open
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system closes the Error Queue (CARD.DEMO.ERROR) using the stored error queue handle
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Error Queue connection is released successfully and the system proceeds to return control to CICS

all_rules.Rule_Name: Close Error Queue During Program Termination
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Error Queue (CARD.DEMO.ERROR) is confirmed to be open at termination time, the system must formally release the connection to the error queue to ensure a clean and complete shutdown.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All open queues (Input, Output/Reply, and Error) have been evaluated and closed as applicable during the termination sequence
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the final step of the termination process
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Control is returned to CICS, the current transaction is ended, and the program terminates completely

all_rules.Rule_Name: Return Control to CICS to End the Transaction
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all open queues have been closed, the program must formally return control to CICS, ending the current transaction and completing the program lifecycle.

description:
CODATE01 is an online CICS program that acts as a message-driven date/time service. It retrieves incoming requests from an MQ input queue, obtains the current system date and time using CICS ASKTIME/FORMATTIME, and places a formatted response message containing the system date and time onto a reply queue. Any processing errors are routed to a dedicated error queue.
- **Execution Environment**: Online (CICS) - **Database Access**: None - **MQ Calls**: Yes - **Module Type**: Main/Driver module
### Key Functionalities: 1: Program Initialization - Initialize working storage fields, clear queue names and message buffers to prepare for processing 2: Open Error Queue - Open the MQ error queue (CARD.DEMO.ERROR) for writing error messages that occur during processing 3: Retrieve Transaction Trigger Information - Retrieve the MQ trigger message from CICS to obtain the input queue name that initiated this transaction 4: Set Input and Reply Queue Names - Set the input queue name from the trigger message and assign the fixed reply queue name (CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE) 5: Open Input Queue - Open the designated input MQ queue for reading incoming date request messages 6: Open Output/Reply Queue - Open the reply MQ queue (CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE) for writing date/time response messages back to requestors 7: Get Request Message - Read the next available request message from the input MQ queue with a 5-second wait interval 8: Save Message Identifiers - Save the message ID, correlation ID, and reply-to queue from the incoming request message for use in the reply 9: Get Current System Date and Time - Retrieve the current system date and time using CICS ASKTIME to obtain the absolute timestamp 10: Format Date and Time - Format the absolute timestamp into MM-DD-YYYY date format and HH:MM:SS time format using CICS FORMATTIME 11: Build Date/Time Reply Message - Construct the reply message string containing the formatted system date and system time (e.g., 'SYSTEM DATE: MM-DD-YYYY SYSTEM TIME: HH:MM:SS') 12: Send Reply Message - Put the date/time reply message onto the output/reply MQ queue, correlating it back to the original request using saved message identifiers 13: Process Message Loop - Continuously retrieve and process date request messages from the input queue until no more messages are available 14: Commit Transaction - Issue a CICS syncpoint to commit each processed message transaction before retrieving the next message 15: Send Error Notification - When an error occurs, write the error details (error description, condition code, reason code, queue name) to the error queue (CARD.DEMO.ERROR) 16: Close Input Queue - Close the input MQ queue upon completion or error to release queue resources 17: Close Output/Reply Queue - Close the output/reply MQ queue upon completion or error to release queue resources 18: Close Error Queue - Close the error MQ queue upon completion or error to release queue resources 19: Program Termination - Return control to CICS after closing all open queues, ending the transaction
